aiTitle: Add Works feature with external links and responsive UI
Add Works feature with external links and responsive UI

content.text:
Using the ‘alpha’ branch as a base…


We now have external link functionality in Songbook Series, Songbook, Song, and Credit People: 
- can we also add it to “Works”, a new grouping/linking feature to link the same song (which may have various versions/arrangements across various sources (songbooks etc). This would work in the same way as “Works” can have multiple Recordings in MusicBrainz. Works can also have ISWC assigned to them. While ISWC will be optional (purely because not all creative works may have a formal ISWC assigned to them), those that do would have one Works record per ISWC
- like in MusicBrainz, can the first field (the dropdown field) in External Links throughout iHymns auto populate based on the link entered. For example, a WikiPedia link auto selects Wikipedia, Facebook link auto selects Facebook etc? This behaviour should be the same throughout iHymns. As this is uniformed functionality, maybe it should be in its own “global module” so that only one change is needed in future and will auto reflect everywhere else?
- the Credits people list view in Manage doesn’t show well on mobiles (see screenshot). Maybe we should remove/Lifespan and Meta columns as part of the responsive design when used on mobiles or other devices with limited horizontal width? Can we also review this elsewhere across the whole of iHymns?



Thoroughly update all our documentation, to reflect this and all other functionality m, including:
- in-app help documentation (visitor and admin/manage)
- markdown repo files (.md)
- swagger/openapi documentation


Create GitHub issues for each of the above. Once each is implemented, Rebase and Commit, then update the individual GitHub Issues comprehensively, before moving onto the next.

Do not create multiple PRs. Only create one at the very end, a single fresh PR to merge to ‘alpha’ branch

commit a006321586b5f66711734fe9e98d25e97a28b2fc
Author: Salem874 <Salem874@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Mon May 4 12:44:17 2026 +0100

    feat(catalogue): MusicBrainz-style external-links system (closes #833) (#837)
    
    * feat(catalogue): external-links schema + backfill migrations (#833)
    
    Three new migrations registered across all four dashboard data
    structures so #820's auto-hide treats them like every other.
    
    migrate-external-links.php — schema:
    - tblExternalLinkTypes (controlled vocabulary registry)
      ~37 seed types via INSERT…ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE keyed on Slug
      (re-runs upsert without touching curator-set IsActive). Categories:
      information / listen / watch / read / sheet-music / purchase /
      authority / official / social / other. AppliesTo is a SET column
      with values song / songbook / person.
    - tblSongbookExternalLinks (FK → tblSongbooks + LinkTypeId)
    - tblSongExternalLinks     (FK → tblSongs     + LinkTypeId)
    - tblCreditPersonExternalLinks (FK → tblCreditPeople + LinkTypeId)
      All three sibling tables: Url VARCHAR(2048), Note, SortOrder,
      Verified flag, Created/Updated timestamps. ON DELETE CASCADE on
      the entity FK; ON DELETE RESTRICT on the LinkType FK.
    
    migrate-backfill-songbook-links.php:
    - Copies non-empty tblSongbooks.WebsiteUrl / InternetArchiveUrl /
      WikipediaUrl into tblSongbookExternalLinks with the corresponding
      link types. NOT EXISTS guard so re-runs are no-ops.
    - Legacy columns NOT dropped — they stay as read-fallbacks.
    
    migrate-backfill-credit-person-links.php:
    - Migrates tblCreditPersonLinks rows into tblCreditPersonExternalLinks.
      Maps free-text LinkType values to controlled-vocabulary slugs
      (wikipedia → wikipedia, imslp → imslp, hymnary → hymnary-org,
      website → official-website, …). Unrecognised values fall through
      to 'other' with the original LinkType preserved in Note. Re-runs
      use NOT EXISTS guard.
    - Legacy tblCreditPersonLinks NOT dropped.
    
    Subsequent commits land:
      - SongData attaches `links` arrays via probe-gated joins
      - Admin UI: songbooks edit modal + credit-people edit modal
        (song-editor UI deferred to a follow-up issue, like #836)
      - Public 'Find this {hymn,songbook,person} elsewhere' panels
      - JSON-LD sameAs on all three page types
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(public): SongData attachment + 'Find elsewhere' panels + JSON-LD sameAs (#833)
    
    SongData side:
    - New _externalLinksMap() helper, generic over the three entity types
      ('songbook' | 'song' | 'person'). Probe-gated on the relevant
      tblXxxExternalLinks table; joins tblExternalLinkTypes and excludes
      rows where IsActive = 0 (soft-deleted link types). Returns a map
      keyed by Abbreviation / SongId / CreditPersonId.
    - getSongbook() / getSongbooks() / _fetchSongRow() attach a `links`
      array carrying {slug, name, category, url, note, verified, iconClass}
      per row, sorted by Category then SortOrder then Name.
    
    Public surfaces:
    - /songbook/<abbr>: 'Find this songbook elsewhere' card with Category
      group headings (Official / Information / Read / Sheet music / Listen
      / Watch / Purchase / Authority / Social / Other), each link
      rendered as an outline button with the seeded Bootstrap icon, the
      optional Note in muted text, and a verified-tick when set.
    - /song/<id>: 'Find this hymn elsewhere' section with the same
      treatment.
    - /people/<slug>: replaces the existing flat 'Links' list with the
      new categorised display when tblCreditPersonExternalLinks has rows;
      legacy tblCreditPersonLinks list still renders as a fallback when
      the new table is empty for the person, so the page never goes dark
      on a deployment that hasn't run the backfill yet.
    
    JSON-LD SEO:
    - MusicComposition.sameAs on /song/<id>.
    - MusicAlbum.sameAs on /songbook/<abbr>.
    - New Person.sameAs on /people/<slug>. Reads from the new table first,
      legacy fallback second (matches the public page's fallback logic).
    
    Pre-migration deployments load every page cleanly — every read path
    short-circuits when the schema isn't there.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(admin): songbook external-links card-list editor (#833)
    
    Edit-modal section:
    - $hasExtLinksSchema probe alongside $hasSeriesSchema.
    - POST /update reads four parallel arrays (ext_link_type_ids[],

{"issues":[{"number":839,"title":"feat(editor): chip-list editor for song external links in /manage/editor","body":"## Goal

Add the **external-links card-list editor** to `/manage/editor/` (the per-song editor) so curators can add / remove / reorder external links for individual songs.

## Why this is a follow-up

Issue #833 / PR #837 shipped:
- `tblSongExternalLinks` schema + the registry it joins to.
- `SongData::_externalLinksMap('song', …)` attaches `links` to song rows.
- `/song/` public page renders the categorised "Find this hymn elsewhere" panel.
- `MusicComposition.sameAs` JSON-LD.

What it didn't do:
- No admin UI to add / edit / remove song-level external links. Curators have to add them via SQL until this lands.

The editor at `appWeb/public_html/manage/editor/index.php` (≈ 1,500 lines) plus `appWeb/public_html/manage/editor/api.php` (≈ 3,000 lines) is a complex code path; landing the card-list editor + the `save_song` reconciliation deserves its own focused PR.

## Scope

### Editor UI
- New "External links" section in the song-edit form.
- Same card-list pattern as the songbook side from #833 / PR #837. Reuse `window._iHymnsLinkTypes` (the seeded type list) and `window._iHymnsBuildExtLinkRow` (the row builder) — both are already exposed on `window` by `manage/songbooks.php`.
- The link-type dropdown should filter to types where `AppliesTo` contains `'song'` (filter the seeded list locally; no extra fetch needed).

### `save_song` API
- Read `ext_link_type_ids[]` + `ext_link_urls[]` + `ext_link_notes[]` + `ext_link_verified[]` parallel arrays from the POST.
- Reconcile via the same DELETE-then-INSERT-in-transaction pattern. Array index → `SortOrder`. Per-row validation: positive type id, non-empty URL ≤ 2048 chars matching `https?://`, note ≤ 255 chars.
- Audit-log entry in `tblActivityLog` for `song.edit` includes `external_link_count`.

### Bulk-import handler
- If a song's JSON payload carries an `externalLinks: [{slug, url, note?, verified?}]` array, write rows during import. Resolve `slug` → `LinkTypeId` once per import (single registry lookup). Idempotent: NOT EXISTS guard or UNIQUE on (SongId, LinkTypeId, Url).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Edit a song → add Hymnary.org, 2 YouTube performances, 1 Spotify, save, reopen → all 4 present in saved order with type / URL / note / verified preserved.
- [ ] Drag-handle reorder persists.
- [ ] Remove a link, save, reopen → gone.
- [ ] `/song/` page picks up the new links on next load (categorised display, icons, etc.).
- [ ] Bulk-import a ZIP whose JSON carries `externalLinks` → rows land in the new table.
- [ ] Pre-#833-migration deployment: editor still saves songs cleanly with the external-links section silently absent.

## Related

- #833 — schema + songbook admin (PR #837).
- #836 — song-editor alternative-titles UI (the song-editor's other deferred admin UI).

- Result: until this follow-up ships, curators see the new categorised public display only for *backfilled* rows; rows added via admin after the backfill ran end up in the legacy table only and surface via the fallback list.

### Option A — Full cutover (preferred)

Replace the existing free-text `LinkType` form with the same card-list editor used in songbooks (PR #837):

Keep the existing form. Extend the save handler to also write to the new table after the legacy insert, using the same slug-mapping logic as the backfill migration. New rows surface in both views; legacy admin still works; cutover happens in a later release.

Probably not worth the maintenance burden — Option A is cleaner. Listed for completeness.

One link-type registry, one consistent admin UI, one public render pattern.

Supports:

- An open-ended **registry of link types** (Hymnary.org, CCLI Songselect, IMSLP, YouTube, Spotify, Internet Archive, Wikipedia, Wikidata, Open Library, OCLC, Hymnal Plus, Cyber Hymnal, LibriVox, Bandcamp, SoundCloud, official site, sheet-music PDF, MusicBrainz artist, Discogs, VIAF, …).
- **Multiple links of the same type** per entity (five different Internet Archive scans of *Christ in Song*; three YouTube performances of *Amazing Grace*; two Wikipedia pages for a person who has both English and German articles).
- Per-link **note / context** (e.g. "1900 first edition scan", "performed by Hillsong Worship 2021", "German Wikipedia article").
- Per-link **verified** flag — curator has eyeballed the URL.
- Coverage for **songs, songbooks AND credit-people** under one schema.
- Sensible **public display** — group by category (Information / Listen / Watch / Read / Sheet music / Purchase / Authority / Official), iconify by type.

Modelled on [MusicBrainz's URL-relationship system](https://musicbrainz.org/relationships/url) which has hundreds of link types and pairs each with the entity types it applies to.

## Why now

- Three hard-coded URL columns can't grow with the catalogue. Internet Archive routinely has 2-5 scans of any given hymnal — there's no slot for the others.
- Songs have **zero** external links today. A discoverer who finds *Amazing Grace* on iHymns has no path to Hymnary.org's deep history, IMSLP's sheet music, the Cyber Hymnal's MIDI, or YouTube performances. Outbound linking is a credibility cue and an SEO win.
- `tblCreditPersonLinks` (from #545) already implements *the same idea* but with `LinkType` as free-text VARCHAR(64), no controlled vocabulary, no shared icon/category metadata. Two parallel systems for one concept = inevitable drift.
- Future structured-data exports (ProPresenter, CCLI, JSON-LD `sameAs`) need typed URLs, not free-text fields.

## Schema (new migrations)

Four normalised tables — one registry + three per-entity join tables:

```sql
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- tblExternalLinkTypes — controlled vocabulary of relationship types.
-- Mirrors MusicBrainz's "link type" registry. Seeded with ~30 types
-- relevant to hymnology + extensible by Global Admin via a future
-- /manage/link-types editor (out of scope for v1 — seed once, edit
-- via SQL until the volume justifies a UI).
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tblExternalLinkTypes (
    Id              INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    Slug            VARCHAR(60)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    Name            VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    Category        ENUM(
                        'information', 'listen', 'watch', 'read',
                        'sheet-music', 'purchase', 'authority',
                        'official', 'social', 'other'
                    ) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'other',
    UrlPattern      VARCHAR(255) NULL,                       -- regex hint for soft validation
    IconClass       VARCHAR(60)  NULL,                       -- bi-* class
    AppliesTo       SET('song','songbook','person') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'song,songbook,person',
    AllowMultiple   TINYINT(1)   NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    IsActive        TINYINT(1)   NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    DisplayOrder    INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    CreatedAt       TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    INDEX idx_active   (IsActive),
    INDEX idx_category (Category, DisplayOrder)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;

-- Per-entity join tables — three siblings of identical shape so the
-- FK constraints stay enforceable per entity-type. A generic
-- EntityType + EntityId pivot would lose those constraints.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tblSongbookExternalLinks (
    Id            INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    SongbookId    INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    LinkTypeId    INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    Url           VARCHAR(2048) NOT NULL,
    Note          VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    SortOrder     INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    Verified      TINYINT(1)   NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    CreatedAt     TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt     TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    INDEX idx_book (SongbookId),
    INDEX idx_type (LinkTypeId),

    FOREIGN KEY fk_link_book      (SongbookId) REFERENCES tblSongbooks(Id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    FOREIGN KEY fk_link_type_book (LinkTypeId) REFERENCES tblExternalLinkTypes(Id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tblSongExternalLinks (
    Id            INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    SongId        VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    LinkTypeId    INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    Url           VARCHAR(2048) NOT NULL,
    Note          VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    SortOrder     INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    Verified      TINYINT(1)   NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    CreatedAt     TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt     TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    INDEX idx_song (SongId),
    INDEX idx_type (LinkTypeId),

    FOREIGN KEY fk_link_song      (SongId)     REFERENCES tblSongs(SongId)         ON DELETE CASCADE,
    FOREIGN KEY fk_link_type_song (LinkTypeId) REFERENCES tblExternalLinkTypes(Id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tblCreditPersonExternalLinks (
    Id              INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    CreditPersonId  INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    LinkTypeId      INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    Url             VARCHAR(2048) NOT NULL,
    Note            VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    SortOrder       INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    Verified        TINYINT(1)   NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    CreatedAt       TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt       TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    INDEX idx_person (CreditPersonId),
    INDEX idx_type   (LinkTypeId),

    FOREIGN KEY fk_link_person      (CreditPersonId) REFERENCES tblCreditPeople(Id)        ON DELETE CASCADE,
    FOREIGN KEY fk_link_type_person (LinkTypeId)     REFERENCES tblExternalLinkTypes(Id)   ON DELETE RESTRICT
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
```

### Migrations

- `migrate-external-links.php` — create the four tables + seed `tblExternalLinkTypes`. Idempotent: re-runs upsert seed rows by slug, never duplicate.
- `migrate-backfill-songbook-links.php` — copy non-empty `tblSongbooks.WebsiteUrl` / `InternetArchiveUrl` / `WikipediaUrl` into `tblSongbookExternalLinks` with the corresponding LinkType.
- `migrate-backfill-credit-person-links.php` — copy every `tblCreditPersonLinks` row into `tblCreditPersonExternalLinks`. Maps the existing free-text `LinkType` strings to registry slugs (most map directly: `wikipedia` → `wikipedia`, `imslp` → `imslp`, `hymnary` → `hymnary-org`, `website` → `official-website`, etc.). Unknown / freeform `LinkType` values map to `other` with the original string preserved in `Note`. Re-running is a no-op (UNIQUE on (CreditPersonId, LinkTypeId, Url) inserts).

**Deprecation, not deletion.** Three legacy reads stay in place for one release cycle:
- `tblSongbooks.WebsiteUrl` / `InternetArchiveUrl` / `WikipediaUrl` — read-paths fall back to these when the new table is empty for a row.
- `tblCreditPersonLinks` — read-paths fall back when the new table is empty for a person.

A separate later migration drops the legacy columns/table once the public site has been on the new system for a release cycle.

Pending-probes (#820) registered for all three migrations, so the dashboard auto-hides them once applied.

1. **Internal search** — a search for *"Faith's Review and Expectation"* should return *Amazing Grace* (its original title); *"Adventist Hymnal"* should return *The Church Hymnal*.

## Why

Songs and songbooks are routinely known by names other than their official one:

- *Amazing Grace* is also "Faith's Review and Expectation" (original 1779 title) and is often searched as "Amazing Grase" (misspelling) or by its full first line.
- *Mission Praise* is widely called "MP" in worship circles.
- *The Church Hymnal* is "the Adventist Hymnal" / "SDA Hymnal" in vernacular.
- Translated hymnals carry their original-language title alongside the local one (*Christ in Song* / *Cristo en el Cántico*).

Today a search for any of those returns nothing, even though the catalogue does have the canonical entry. Worse, search engines only index the canonical name, so a Google search for the alt name doesn't find iHymns at all.

-- multilingual hymns ('en-GB' for old English variants, 'es' for the

    Id           INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    SongId       VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,                  -- canonical 'CP-0001' id
    Title        VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    Language     VARCHAR(35)  NULL,                       -- IETF BCP 47, optional
    SortOrder    INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    Note         VARCHAR(255) NULL,                       -- e.g. "original title", "common misspelling"
    CreatedAt    TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    INDEX idx_title  (Title),                             -- supports LIKE search
    UNIQUE KEY uq_song_title (SongId, Title),             -- no duplicates per song

    FOREIGN KEY fk_alt_song (SongId) REFERENCES tblSongs(SongId) ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tblSongbookAlternativeTitles (

    SongbookId   INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,                   -- tblSongbooks.Id
    Title        VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    SortOrder    INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    Note         VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    CreatedAt    TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    INDEX idx_book    (SongbookId),
    INDEX idx_title   (Title),
    UNIQUE KEY uq_book_title (SongbookId, Title),

    FOREIGN KEY fk_alt_book (SongbookId) REFERENCES tblSongbooks(Id) ON DELETE CASCADE

## Search integration

### Server-side (api.php `action=search`)
- `UNION` the existing `tblSongs.Title LIKE ?` query with `tblSongAlternativeTitles.Title LIKE ?`, deduplicating by `SongId`.
- When the match was via an alt title, attach `matched_via: { alternative_title: "" }` to the result row so the UI can render the hint.

### Client-side (Fuse.js index)
- `exportAsJson()` adds an `alternativeTitles: ["…", "…"]` array to each song row and an `alternativeNames: […]` array to each songbook row.
- Fuse.js index includes those keys with reduced weight (~0.5× of the canonical title) so a match on the canonical name still ranks higher.

### Result UI
- When a search row matched on an alt title, render "(known as: )" muted-grey under the canonical line.

Add an optional **Compiler** credit field to a Songbook to record the person (or people) who compiled / edited / curated the published collection. This is a credit at the **songbook** level — distinct from the existing per-song credits (writer / composer / arranger / adaptor / translator / artist).

## Why

A hymnal is curated work in its own right. *Mission Praise* was compiled by **Peter Horrobin & Greg Leavers**. *Christ in Song* by **Frank E. Belden**. *The Church Hymnal* by editorial committees that change with every edition. That information belongs on the songbook, not buried as a "publisher" footnote, and not duplicated across every song. Having it as a structured credit unlocks:

- Public songbook page can render *"Compiled by …"* alongside Publisher / Publication year / Affiliation.
- Future ProPresenter / CCLI exports can include the compiler in proper-attribution metadata.
- Compiler people get a `/people/` page just like song writers do (via `tblCreditPeople`), with their compiled songbooks listed as their "discography".

## Schema

Reuse the existing `tblCreditPeople` registry — same shape as song credits — via a new join table:

    Id              INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    SongbookId      INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    CreditPersonId  INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    SortOrder       INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    Note            VARCHAR(255) NULL,        -- e.g. "5th edition", "with B. Smith"
    CreatedAt       TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    UNIQUE KEY uq_book_person (SongbookId, CreditPersonId),
    INDEX idx_book   (SongbookId),
    INDEX idx_person (CreditPersonId),

    FOREIGN KEY fk_compiler_book   (SongbookId)     REFERENCES tblSongbooks(Id)    ON DELETE CASCADE,
    FOREIGN KEY fk_compiler_person (CreditPersonId) REFERENCES tblCreditPeople(Id) ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;

","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"Salem874"},"labels":["enhancement","admin","songbooks","data-migration"],"comments":1,"created_at":"2026-05-03T22:14:40Z","updated_at":"2026-05-03T23:06:04Z"},{"number":822,"title":"feat(pwa): pull-down-to-refresh gesture for native-style refresh on installed PWA","body":"## Goal

Native-app-style **pull-down-to-refresh** gesture for the iHymns PWA. When the user is at the top of a scrollable page and pulls the page down past a threshold, fire a refresh of the current view (re-fetch song data, songbooks, notifications, whatever the page consumes) with a visible progress indicator that mirrors what iOS Safari / Chrome on Android show natively.

## Why

PWAs in standalone mode (the way iHymns is launched once installed) **don't get the OS browser's built-in pull-to-refresh** — it's a feature of the browser chrome that the standalone PWA hides. Users who installed iHymns as an app expect the same gesture they get in any other native app and currently have no equivalent (no menu refresh button on `/`, no keyboard shortcut on mobile).

Adding it ourselves restores parity with native expectations and gives a reliable way to get fresh data after sync, without the user having to leave the app and come back.

## Scope

- **Pure web** — implement in vanilla JS as a module under `appWeb/public_html/js/modules/`. No new dependencies.
- **Touch + mouse** — primarily touch-driven, but `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup` so the same code path covers mouse-drag on a non-touch laptop in dev tools.
- **Trigger surface** — only at the very top of a scrollable area (`scrollTop === 0`). Mid-page scrolls and horizontal swipes are not consumed; the gesture only kicks in when there's nowhere left to scroll up.
- **Pages**: home (`/`), songbooks listing, song page, search results, settings, notifications, set lists. Anywhere the user might want fresh data.
- **NOT** wired to admin pages (`/manage/*`) for v1 — those are PHP full-page-reload surfaces; a browser refresh works fine. Re-evaluate after v1 lands.
- **Visual**: a subtle pull indicator at the top of the page that grows with the gesture, snapping to a "release to refresh" affordance once past the threshold; spinner during the refresh; auto-dismiss on completion.
- **Refresh action**: dispatches a `ihymns:refresh-requested` custom event the page's main controller listens for. Each page decides what "refresh" means — re-fetch songbooks for the home grid, re-poll notifications, re-run the song-data fetch, etc. No global "reload window" hack.

## Implementation sketch

```js
// js/modules/pull-to-refresh.js
export class PullToRefresh {
  constructor({ threshold = 70, scrollContainer = document.scrollingElement } = {}) { ... }
  init() {
    /* attach pointerdown on scrollContainer, track delta, only engage
       when scrollTop === 0 && pointer is moving downward. Show
       indicator. Past threshold + release → dispatch event +
       show spinner; below threshold + release → snap back. */
  }
}
```

```js
// In each page's controller (e.g. home.js):
document.addEventListener('ihymns:refresh-requested', async () => {
  await this.songData.refresh();
  this.render();
  document.dispatchEvent(new Event('ihymns:refresh-complete'));
});
```

The PullToRefresh module hides its spinner when `ihymns:refresh-complete` fires (with a timeout safety net at ~5 s so a hung handler still un-stuck the UI).

## Acceptance

- [ ] On installed PWA (iOS / Android / desktop standalone), pulling down past threshold at top-of-page triggers visible refresh affordance.
- [ ] Below threshold + release → snaps back, no refresh fired.
- [ ] At mid-page (scrollTop > 0) → gesture not consumed; native scroll behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] Refresh fires the page's data-refresh path; spinner clears on completion or after 5s timeout.
- [ ] Works in browser tab too (mouse drag from top), so dev / debug doesn't need a phone.
- [ ] Accessibility: doesn't break keyboard navigation, screen-reader announce on refresh start / complete.
- [ ] Disabled at admin / editor surfaces (`/manage/*`, `/manage/editor/`) — those are full-page reload PHP surfaces.

## Out of scope

- Background refresh / pull-to-load-more pagination.
- Per-page custom indicator content (everyone gets the same spinner).
- Haptics — no Web Vibration API call from v1; native PWA shells already provide it on supported platforms.

## Status

Filed as a follow-up to PR #821 (admin polish + bug-fix batch). Standalone PR.
","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"Salem874"},"labels":["enhancement","platform-web","ux","pwa"],"comments":1,"created_at":"2026-05-03T14:10:09Z","updated_at":"2026-05-03T17:31:12Z"},{"number":820,"title":"feat(setup-database): auto-hide migrations whose work is already fully applied (only show pending)","body":"## Goal

Hide migration cards from `/manage/setup-database` whose work is already fully applied. Only the cards an admin **needs to act on** stay visible by default; "everything already done" rolls up into a single expander.

## Why

The Database Setup page lists every migration ever shipped — including ones that will no-op every time after their first successful run. Admins scanning for "what do I need to apply after this deploy?" have to read 25+ cards to find the 1-2 that are pending. The information is implicit in each script's `[skip]` log lines but isn't surfaced to the UI.

## Approach

Each migration script gets a lightweight `is_pending()` probe that returns `true | false` based on `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` checks — does the column / table / row exist, does the index match, etc. The dashboard calls every probe before rendering and:

1. **Pending cards** render normally at the top of the grid.
2. **Already-applied cards** roll into a `` block: *"21 migrations already applied — show details"*. Expanding reveals them so an admin can still re-run for diagnostics.
3. **Always-on operation cards** (Install / Migrate Song Data / Cleanup / Backup / Restore / Drop Legacy) stay visible regardless.

Probe is opt-in per migration — scripts that don't expose `migration_*_is_pending()` keep current behaviour (always render).

## Implementation sketch

```php
// In each migrate-*.php:
function migration_bulk_import_jobs_is_pending(mysqli $db): bool
{
    $r = $db->query(
        "SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.TABLES
          WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE() AND TABLE_NAME = 'tblBulkImportJobs' LIMIT 1"
    );
    return $r === false || $r->num_rows === 0;
}

// In setup-database.php:
$pendingActions = [];
$appliedActions = [];
foreach ($migrationOrder as $action) {
    $probe = "migration_" . str_replace('-', '_', $action) . "_is_pending";
    require_once $scriptDir . $scriptMap[$action];   // brings probe into scope
    if (function_exists($probe) && $probe($db)) {
        $pendingActions[] = $action;
    } else {
        $appliedActions[] = $action;
    }
}
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] On a fully-up-to-date database, every migration card collapses into the "already applied" expander; only operation cards (Install / etc.) and the "Apply all" banner remain visible.
- [ ] After a deploy that lands new migrations, those cards render at the top in dependency order.
- [ ] After running each pending migration successfully, the card moves into the expander automatically (the next page load reflects the change).
- [ ] An admin can still expand the panel and click any applied card for a forced re-run (idempotent — they no-op).
- [ ] Probes are bounded — adding 30 probes runs in under 100 ms cumulatively (single connection, prepared statement reuse).

## Status

**Deferred — follow-up to the current admin-batch-polish PR.** Implementing this requires touching every migration script to add a probe, and is best done as a focused pass once the rest of the admin-polish work has shipped.

## Related

- #NEW-6 (re-label migration cards) — lands first; this builds on the new card grid.
- #NEW-8 (drop redundant SongCount Recompute card) — same direction (less clutter); this generalises the principle.
- #518 — schema-audit page; conceptually adjacent but its surface is "is the schema healthy?" not "what's pending?".

The `/manage` sidebar has grown to 24 entries across 4 group headings (Content / People / Operations / Help) plus the top-level Dashboard. Scanning for a destination requires reading the whole list. Convert both the desktop sidebar (`appWeb/public_html/manage/includes/admin-sidebar.php`) and the mobile offcanvas hamburger (`appWeb/public_html/manage/includes/admin-nav.php` `#admin-nav-offcanvas` block) to **collapsible accordion sections**.

Default state: every group **collapsed** except the group containing the active page. The active group expands automatically so the user can see their position; sibling groups stay tucked away.

Section dividers as the accordion toggles:

- **Dashboard** (top-level, no group)
- ▸ **Songs** — Song Editor · Song Requests · Revisions Audit · Missing Numbers · Song Link Suggestions
- ▸ **Catalogue** — Songbooks · Songbook Series · Credit People · Languages · Tags & Themes
- ▸ **Access** — Content Restrictions · Access Tiers · Entitlements
- ▸ **People** — Users · User Groups · Organisations · My Organisations
- ▸ **Operations** — Analytics · CCLI Usage Report · Data Health · Activity Log · Schema Audit · Database Setup · Configuration · Notifications
- ▸ **Help** — Help / Guides

(The current "Content" group splits into Songs / Catalogue / Access. Entitlements moves to Access since it controls who-can-do-what. Notifications joins Operations once #NEW-3 ships.)

## Implementation

- The link registry at `appWeb/public_html/manage/includes/admin-links.php` already carries a `group` field on every entry. Extend the value set to the seven groups above. Order of first appearance defines render order.
- Use Bootstrap 5 `.accordion` markup so the same component works for sidebar + offcanvas.
- Each collapsed section persists its open/closed state in `localStorage` keyed by group name. Active page's group is always force-expanded on page load.
- Group header click toggles; chevron icon reflects state (down = expanded, right = collapsed).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Desktop sidebar shows seven collapsible groups; only the active group is expanded by default.
- [ ] Mobile hamburger offcanvas mirrors the same structure with the same accordion behaviour.
- [ ] Collapsing / expanding a group on either surface persists across navigations within the same session.
- [ ] Active page's group always opens on first page load regardless of stored preference.
- [ ] Keyboard navigation still works: Tab through groups; Enter / Space to toggle; Tab into expanded entries.
- [ ] No regression on entitlement gating — items hidden by `userHasEntitlement()` still don't render.

## Out of scope

- A search-the-sidebar input. Tracked separately if the sidebar continues to grow.
- Re-skinning the icons. Icons stay as-is.

input.title: feat(catalogue): introduce Works (group of song versions across sources, with optional ISWC + external links)
input.body:
## Goal

Introduce a new top-level catalogue entity — **Works** — that groups multiple `tblSongs` rows that represent the same underlying composition across different sources (different songbooks, different arrangements, different translations, etc.).

Conceptually mirrors **MusicBrainz Works** ↔ **Recordings** (one Work, many Recordings / one Work, many `tblSongs`).

## Why

We already let curators link counterparts pairwise across songbooks (#807 / #808). That covers _"this AMNS song is the same as this NEH song"_, but it doesn't give the song a single name in the registry, doesn't let downstream tools (CCLI tooling, external-links curation, the public site's discovery surfaces) treat the family as one thing, and it doesn't let us record an **ISWC** (the international standard code for musical works) once and have it apply to every source row.

Going Works-shaped also future-proofs:
- one canonical title + one canonical credit set per Work (and from there, per-song overrides)
- one external-links panel ("Find this hymn elsewhere") that aggregates from every member song
- future MusicBrainz / ISWCNet integration via the ISWC

## Scope

### Schema (new migration `migrate-works.php`, idempotent)
- **`tblWorks`**:
  - `Id INT UNSIGNED PK AUTO_INCREMENT`
  - `Iswc CHAR(15) NULL UNIQUE` — `T-NNN.NNN.NNN-C` formatted; **optional** because not every creative work has a formally registered ISWC
  - `Title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL` — canonical / preferred title
  - `Slug VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL UNIQUE` — URL-safe handle, derived from Title (uniquified with `-2`, `-3` etc. when collisions occur)
  - `Notes TEXT NULL`
  - `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt` timestamps
  - Index on `Title`, on `Iswc`
- **`tblWorkSongs`** (membership):
  - `WorkId INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL` (FK → `tblWorks.Id` ON DELETE CASCADE)
  - `SongId VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL` (FK → `tblSongs.SongId` ON DELETE CASCADE)
  - `IsCanonical TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` — flag the "preferred" song-row for the Work (zero or one per Work)
  - `Note VARCHAR(255) NULL`
  - `CreatedAt` timestamp
  - PK `(WorkId, SongId)` so a song can only belong once to a given work; we DO allow the same song to belong to multiple Works only if a curator deliberately wants that (rare — usually a misclassification).
- **`tblWorkExternalLinks`**: same shape as the per-entity tables introduced in #833 — `WorkId / LinkTypeId / Url / Note / SortOrder / Verified / CreatedAt / UpdatedAt`. FK on `WorkId` ON DELETE CASCADE; FK on `LinkTypeId` ON DELETE RESTRICT.
- **`tblExternalLinkTypes.AppliesTo`** — extend the SET to include `'work'` so the registry can flag types that apply to Works (most do, but e.g. the "find a grave" type only applies to people).
- **No legacy backfill** — Works is brand new, nothing to migrate from. The migration registers in the four dashboards (admin home, my-organisations, manage index, setup-database) like every other migration since #820.

### Read path — `SongData`
- New `_worksMap()` helper, parallel to `_externalLinksMap()`. Probe-gated on `tblWorks` existing.
- For each song row, attach a `works` array `[ { id, title, slug, iswc, isCanonical, members: [{songId, songbookAbbr, number, title}], links: [...] } ]`. Members are the sibling songs in the same Work, sorted by SongbookAbbr / Number.
- `getWork($workIdOrSlug)` for the public Work page.

### Public surfaces
- New route **`/work/<slug>`** rendered via `includes/pages/work.php`:
  - Title + ISWC (with link to ISWCNet if set), notes
  - **"Versions across sources"** list — every member song, grouped by songbook
  - **"Find this work elsewhere"** panel — categorised external links, exactly like the song / songbook / person pages from #833
  - **JSON-LD `MusicComposition.sameAs`** mirroring the song page treatment
- On `/song/<id>`: if the song belongs to a Work, render a small "Part of work — _<work title>_" line that links to `/work/<slug>`, plus a "Other versions of this work" sub-list when there are siblings.
- On `/people/<slug>`: when the credit-set of a Work matches the person, the Work-level title appears alongside their songs (de-duplicates noise — currently the person page lists every per-songbook copy of the same hymn).

### Admin — new page `manage/works.php`
- List view (with the responsive treatment from the new mobile-list issue), filterable by title / ISWC / member-count / has-links-or-not.
- New / edit modal with:
  - Title, ISWC (optional, validate the `T-NNN.NNN.NNN-C` shape if supplied)
  - Slug (auto-derived but editable)
  - Notes
  - **Members picker** — typeahead over `tblSongs.SongId` / Title / SongbookAbbr; cards stack with drag-handle reorder; "Mark as canonical" radio (zero or one per Work)
  - **External links** — same card-list editor pattern shipped in #833 (re-use `window._iHymnsLinkTypes` + `window._iHymnsBuildExtLinkRow`)
- Audit-log every create / update / delete with `external_link_count`, `member_count`, ISWC presence.
- Bulk action: "Group counterparts as a Work" — given a set of song-counterpart pairs from #807 / #808, materialise the inferred connected component as a new Work in one click.

### Cross-link housekeeping
- When a song is deleted: `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `tblWorkSongs` removes the membership row. If that leaves a Work with zero members, the Work itself is _not_ auto-deleted (curator decides). Surface a "Works with no members" filter in the admin list.

### Editor (`/manage/editor/`)
- On the song-edit form: a **"Works"** picker — typeahead over `tblWorks.Title` / `Iswc`, plus a **"+ Create new Work from this song"** shortcut.
- Same `save_song` reconciliation pattern: parallel arrays for `work_ids[]`, DELETE-then-INSERT in transaction.

### API
- Extend `/api?action=song` payload with `works` (mirrors what `SongData` attaches).
- New `/api?action=work&slug=…` returning the same shape as the public page consumes.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)
- ISWC remote validation against ISWCNet (we'll just shape-validate + curator-trust for now).
- Bulk import of Works from CCLI / MusicBrainz dumps.
- Per-Work credit overrides — we read credits from the canonical member song.

## Done when
- Migration applies cleanly on a fresh install + on a deployment that already has #833 applied.
- Pre-migration deployments still load every page (probe-gated everywhere).
- `/work/<slug>` renders for a manually-seeded Work; admin can create / edit / delete Works; song-edit can attach the song to one or more Works.
- Setup-database card auto-hides once the schema is applied (same pattern as #820).
- Documentation updated alongside (in-app help, `.md` files, OpenAPI).

input.title: feat(catalogue): auto-detect external-link provider from URL (single global module reused everywhere)
input.body:
## Goal

When a curator pastes a URL into an external-links row anywhere in iHymns, the **provider dropdown** should auto-select the correct registry entry (`tblExternalLinkTypes.Slug`).

Behaviour mirrors **MusicBrainz**: paste a Wikipedia URL → "Wikipedia" auto-selected; paste a Facebook URL → "Facebook"; paste a Spotify URL → "Spotify"; paste a YouTube URL → "YouTube"; etc.

If the curator has already explicitly chosen a non-`other` provider, we don't overwrite it (their choice wins). If the URL doesn't match anything, leave the dropdown alone.

## Why

- The current edit-modals (songbooks today, credit-people / songs / works as the rest of #838 / #839 / #840 land) force the curator to scroll the long grouped dropdown for the right entry every single time, even though the URL almost always uniquely identifies the provider.
- Two screens, two implementations, two places to fix bugs is a smell. Centralise once now while we have only one concrete consumer.

## Approach — single global module

Create **`appWeb/public_html/js/modules/external-link-detect.js`**:

```js
// Exposed on window as window.iHymnsLinkDetect
//
// detectFromUrl(url) -> slug | null
//   Returns the registry slug that matches the URL, or null.
//
// attachAutoDetect(rowEl, opts) -> teardown fn
//   Wires a row's URL input + provider <select> together. Idempotent.
//   opts.respectManualChoice (default true) — don't overwrite a non-default
//   provider that the curator picked manually (tracked via a data-attr the
//   <select> stamps on `change`).
```

The matcher is a hostname / path-pattern table keyed by slug. Initial coverage (mirrors the seeded `tblExternalLinkTypes` from #833):

| slug | hostname / pattern |
| --- | --- |
| `wikipedia` | `*.wikipedia.org` |
| `wikidata` | `wikidata.org`, `www.wikidata.org` |
| `hymnary-org` | `hymnary.org` |
| `hymnal-plus` | `hymnalplus.com` |
| `cyber-hymnal` | `hymntime.com`, `cyberhymnal.org` |
| `internet-archive` | `archive.org` |
| `open-library` | `openlibrary.org` |
| `oclc-worldcat` | `worldcat.org` |
| `viaf` | `viaf.org` |
| `loc-name-authority` | `id.loc.gov` |
| `find-a-grave` | `findagrave.com` |
| `ccli-songselect` | `songselect.ccli.com` |
| `imslp` | `imslp.org` |
| `youtube` | `youtube.com`, `youtu.be`, `m.youtube.com` (but **not** `music.youtube.com` — that's `youtube-music`) |
| `vimeo` | `vimeo.com` |
| `spotify` | `open.spotify.com`, `spotify.com` |
| `apple-music` | `music.apple.com` |
| `youtube-music` | `music.youtube.com` |
| `bandcamp` | `*.bandcamp.com` |
| `soundcloud` | `soundcloud.com` |
| `librivox` | `librivox.org` |
| `discogs` | `discogs.com` |
| `musicbrainz-work` | `musicbrainz.org/work/` |
| `musicbrainz-recording` | `musicbrainz.org/recording/` |
| `musicbrainz-artist` | `musicbrainz.org/artist/` |
| `goodreads-author` | `goodreads.com/author/` |
| `linkedin` | `linkedin.com/in/`, `linkedin.com/company/` |
| `twitter-x` | `twitter.com`, `x.com` |
| `instagram` | `instagram.com` |
| `facebook` | `facebook.com`, `m.facebook.com`, `fb.com` |
| `mastodon` | mastodon-server detection: hostname starts with `@` path or is in a known mastodon-instance allowlist |

Hostname matching uses `URL.hostname` and is case-insensitive. The path-discriminated MusicBrainz / LinkedIn / Goodreads entries match on `pathname` prefix.

Order matters — more-specific rules (e.g. MusicBrainz path-prefixes; `music.youtube.com`) must be checked before less-specific (`youtube.com`).

## Wiring

The module is loaded once in `manage/includes/head-libs.php` (so every admin page gets it without explicit `<script>` tags per-page). The existing per-page edit-modal scripts call `window.iHymnsLinkDetect.attachAutoDetect(rowEl)` inside the row builder (`window._iHymnsBuildExtLinkRow` from #833).

Because the public site doesn't edit anything, we don't load it on the visitor side.

## Manual-choice override

Stamp `data-user-picked="1"` on the `<select>` once the user manually changes it. The detector reads that attr and bails when set. A "Reset auto-detect" button on the row can clear the attr if the curator changes their mind.

## Testing

- Unit tests under `tests/js/external-link-detect.test.js` covering each row in the table + a few edge cases:
  - `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo` → `wikipedia`
  - `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc` → `youtube`
  - `https://music.youtube.com/playlist?list=…` → `youtube-music` (NOT `youtube`)
  - `https://example.com/random` → `null`
  - empty string → `null`
  - malformed URL → `null` (catches `URL` constructor throw)
  - leading/trailing whitespace → trimmed before matching

- Module exists, exported on `window.iHymnsLinkDetect`.
- Wired into the songbook edit-modal row builder; pasting a URL flips the dropdown.
- Wired into credit-people / works / song editor as those land (#838 / #840 / #839).
- Documentation updated alongside.

input.title: refactor(admin): responsive list views — hide low-value columns on narrow viewports (Credit People + audit)
input.body:
## Goal

The `/manage/credit-people` list view doesn't render well on phones (see screenshot). The "Lifespan" and "Meta" columns push the table off-screen and force horizontal scrolling; on iPhone the right-most cells get clipped entirely.

Apply a consistent **mobile-first responsive treatment** across every admin list view: drop low-value columns below a breakpoint, surface their data via a tooltip / expandable row instead.

## Approach

### Convention
Mark each `<th>` / `<td>` with one of:
- `data-col-priority="primary"` — never hidden (Name, Roles, action buttons)
- `data-col-priority="secondary"` — hidden below `≤ 768px` (Lifespan, Meta, Total uses)
- `data-col-priority="tertiary"` — hidden below `≤ 992px` (audit timestamps, IDs)

A small global stylesheet rule in `appWeb/public_html/css/admin.css` (or wherever the manage CSS lives) hides these via media queries — no JS needed.

The columns currently visible on `/manage/credit-people` map as:
- Name → primary
- Roles → primary
- Total uses → primary (it's the most-asked-after metric)
- Source → secondary
- Lifespan → secondary
- Meta → tertiary

### Surfacing the hidden info
On a narrow viewport, expose the hidden columns by:
- A **chevron expand** button on each row that flips a hidden details strip below it. Cheap, zero JS deps.
- Alternatively, just display the hidden values inline in the primary cell on narrow viewports (small muted text under the Name). Simpler; we don't have to wire JS.

Recommendation: inline-under-name on narrow, table-columns on wide. (See the home-page card layout from #807 for prior art.)

### Pages to touch (audit)

Walk every `/manage/*.php` page that renders a `<table>` list. Apply the same priority data-attrs:
- [ ] `manage/credit-people.php` (the screenshot motivator)
- [ ] `manage/songbooks.php`
- [ ] `manage/songbook-series.php`
- [ ] `manage/works.php` (new from #840 — set the convention from day one)
- [ ] `manage/users.php`
- [ ] `manage/organisations.php`
- [ ] `manage/groups.php`
- [ ] `manage/tiers.php`
- [ ] `manage/tags.php`
- [ ] `manage/languages.php`
- [ ] `manage/missing-numbers.php`
- [ ] `manage/song-link-suggestions.php`
- [ ] `manage/requests.php`
- [ ] `manage/notifications.php`
- [ ] `manage/activity-log.php` — high-density, especially benefits
- [ ] `manage/ccli-report.php`
- [ ] `manage/data-health.php`
- [ ] `manage/restrictions.php`
- [ ] `manage/revisions.php`
- [ ] `manage/schema-audit.php`

Visitor-side too: walk `includes/pages/*.php` and apply the convention to any `<table>`-based list (songbooks index, person index, etc.).

## Done when
- On viewport `≤ 414px` (iPhone portrait), `/manage/credit-people` renders without horizontal-scroll.
- The convention is documented in `DEV_NOTES.md` ("admin list-view responsive convention") so the next page added inherits it for free.
- Documentation updated alongside (in-app help screenshots / admin guide).

input.title: docs: comprehensive refresh of in-app help, repo .md files, and OpenAPI/Swagger
input.body:
## Goal

Bring all three documentation surfaces back in sync with the platform as it stands today, including the new external-links system (#833), Works (#840), URL auto-detect (#841), and responsive admin list views (#842).

## Surface 1 — In-app help

### Visitor help (`includes/pages/help.php` + `/help/*.md`)
- Add a **"Find this hymn / songbook / person elsewhere"** section explaining the new categorised external-links panels (Official / Information / Read / Sheet music / Listen / Watch / Purchase / Authority / Social / Other), how to read the verified-tick, and how to suggest corrections via Request a Song.
- Add a **Works** section: what a Work is (the same composition appearing in multiple songbooks / arrangements / translations), how the `/work/<slug>` page is laid out, and the relationship between Work + ISWC + member songs.
- Update **Songbooks**, **Songs**, **Credit People** sections to mention the new external-links surfaces and the cross-linking they enable.
- Update screenshots where the visible UI has changed.

### Admin / curator help (`manage/help.php`)
- New **"External links"** section — the controlled vocabulary, how to add a row (now with auto-detect from URL — #841), how Verified ticks work, what each Category means, and the legacy-fallback behaviour while we keep `tblCreditPersonLinks` / songbook URL columns as read fallbacks for one release cycle.
- New **"Works"** section — how to create a Work, attach member songs, mark a canonical version, set ISWC (and the format we expect), the bulk "group counterparts" flow.
- New **"Mobile admin"** section briefly noting the responsive convention from #842 (which columns drop below which breakpoint, and how to expand the hidden info).
- Refresh **"Catalogue overview"** to include Works + the new external-links system in the entity-relationship diagram.

## Surface 2 — Repo `.md` files

- `README.md` — feature bullets refreshed; new section pointing to in-app help; mention Works in the elevator pitch.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (root + `appWeb/CHANGELOG.md`) — entries for #833, #835, #834, #840, #841, #842, plus this docs PR.
- `DEV_NOTES.md` — document:
  - The external-links data shape (registry + per-entity link tables) and how `SongData::_externalLinksMap` joins it.
  - The Works data shape + `_worksMap` helper.
  - The URL-auto-detect module's exported API + how to add a new provider rule (one-place change).
  - The admin list-view responsive convention (data-col-priority="primary|secondary|tertiary" + breakpoints).
  - The "soft drop" pattern we use for legacy columns we keep as read-fallbacks for one release.
- `Project_Plan.md` — tick off completed items, add Works follow-ups (ISWCNet remote validation, MusicBrainz dump import).
- `PROJECT_STATUS.md` — current-quarter progress refreshed.
- `wiki/*.md` — refresh any pages that reference the catalogue model (entity overview, admin guide).
- `help/*.md` — mirror the in-app help updates.

## Surface 3 — OpenAPI / Swagger (`appWeb/public_html/api-docs.yaml`)

- Add `Work` schema:
  - `id`, `title`, `slug`, `iswc` (nullable), `notes` (nullable), `members` (array of song refs), `links` (array of external-link entries).
- Add `ExternalLink` shared schema (`{ slug, name, category, url, note, verified, iconClass }`) and reference it from existing `Song`, `Songbook`, `Person` schemas where the runtime payload now carries `links`.
- Add the `/api?action=work&slug=…` endpoint.
- Update `/api?action=song` and `/api?action=songbook` and `/api?action=person` payload examples to include the new `links` array.
- Document `tblExternalLinkTypes.AppliesTo` accepting `'work'` (#840 extends the SET).

## Done when
- Visitor help renders the new sections without broken anchors.
- Admin help renders the new sections.
- `CHANGELOG.md` lists every shipped feature this PR cycle.
- `api-docs.yaml` validates against the OpenAPI 3 spec (no schema errors).
- Cross-links between the three surfaces all resolve (no 404s, no stale hash links).

/* ParentWorkId is a nullable self-FK with ON DELETE SET NULL — when
       a parent work is deleted, child works "orphan" cleanly rather
       than cascading away. The depth of the nesting is unconstrained
       (mirrors MusicBrainz, which allows arbitrary parent/child trees:
       original work → arrangement → translation → choral arrangement
       → …). The admin UI surfaces a tree view; cycle detection is
       enforced application-side at update time (DB-level cycle
       prevention would need stored procedures we don't otherwise rely
       on). */
    $sql = "CREATE TABLE tblWorks (
        Id            INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
        ParentWorkId  INT UNSIGNED NULL,
        Iswc          CHAR(15)     NULL,
        Title         VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
        Slug          VARCHAR(80)  NOT NULL,
        Notes         TEXT         NULL,
        CreatedAt     TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        UpdatedAt     TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

        UNIQUE KEY uq_slug   (Slug),
        UNIQUE KEY uq_iswc   (Iswc),
        INDEX      idx_title (Title),
        INDEX      idx_parent (ParentWorkId),

        CONSTRAINT fk_work_parent
            FOREIGN KEY (ParentWorkId) REFERENCES tblWorks(Id) ON DELETE SET NULL
    ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci";

input.body:
### Update — unlimited Work nesting

Like MusicBrainz, Works can also be nested — an original Work can have a child Work that's a different arrangement / translation / choral version, that child can in turn have its own children, etc. with unlimited depth.

Reflected in the schema as a self-referential nullable FK:

```sql
ParentWorkId INT UNSIGNED NULL,
INDEX idx_parent (ParentWorkId),
CONSTRAINT fk_work_parent
    FOREIGN KEY (ParentWorkId) REFERENCES tblWorks(Id) ON DELETE SET NULL
```

`ON DELETE SET NULL` so deleting a parent orphans children cleanly rather than cascading them away. Cycle detection (no Work can be its own ancestor) is enforced application-side at update time.

Admin UI surfaces a tree view in the list + breadcrumb on the edit modal; the public `/work/<slug>` page renders parent / sibling / child links so visitors can navigate the family.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

/**
 * iHymns — Credit Person Public Page (#588)
 *
 * Copyright (c) 2026 iHymns. All rights reserved.
 *
 * PURPOSE:
 * Public landing page for a `tblCreditPeople` registry row. Surfaces
 * the bio, lifespan, special-case / group classification, external
 * links, and a discography grouped by role across the six song-credit
 * tables.
 *
 * Loaded via api.php?page=person&slug=cecil-frances-humphreys-alexander.
 * Expects $personSlug to be set by api.php before inclusion.
 *
 * Falls back to /writer/<slug> behaviour for installs that haven't
 * applied the migrate-credit-people-slug migration yet — the slug
 * lookup short-circuits to a name-based search across the credit
 * tables, so the page still works even before the registry row
 * exists.
 */

require_once __DIR__ . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . '..' . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . 'db_mysql.php';

/**
 * Slug → display name when no registry row exists. Mirrors the
 * /writer/<slug> page's fallback behaviour.
 */
function _personSlugToName(string $slug): string
{
    $slug = urldecode($slug);
    return mb_convert_case(str_replace('-', ' ', $slug), MB_CASE_TITLE, 'UTF-8');
}

$person = null;            /* tblCreditPeople row, or null on partial install / unknown slug */
$personName = '';          /* always set — falls back to slug-derived name */
$db = getDbMysqli();

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 1. Look up the registry row (if the migration has been applied).       */
/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */
try {
    $stmt = $db->prepare(
        "SELECT Id, Name, Notes, BirthPlace, BirthDate, DeathPlace, DeathDate,
                COALESCE(IsSpecialCase, 0) AS IsSpecialCase,
                COALESCE(IsGroup, 0)        AS IsGroup
           FROM tblCreditPeople
          WHERE Slug = ?
          LIMIT 1"
    );
    if ($stmt) {
        $stmt->bind_param('s', $personSlug);
        $stmt->execute();
        $row = $stmt->get_result()->fetch_assoc();
        $stmt->close();
        if ($row) {
            $person = $row;
            $personName = (string)$row['Name'];
        }
    }
} catch (\Throwable $_e) {
    /* Slug column doesn't exist yet (pre-migration) — fall through to
       the name-based fallback below. */
}

/* No registry row matched → derive the display name from the slug. */
if ($personName === '') {
    $personName = _personSlugToName($personSlug);
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* 2. Discography by role — count + list across all six credit tables.    */
/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */
$roleTables = [
    'writer'     => ['table' => 'tblSongWriters',     'label' => 'As Writer',      'icon' => 'fa-pen-fancy'],
    'composer'   => ['table' => 'tblSongComposers',   'label' => 'As Composer',    'icon' => 'fa-music'],
    'arranger'   => ['table' => 'tblSongArrangers',   'label' => 'As Arranger',    'icon' => 'fa-sliders'],
    'adaptor'    => ['table' => 'tblSongAdaptors',    'label' => 'As Adaptor',     'icon' => 'fa-compact-disc'],
    'translator' => ['table' => 'tblSongTranslators', 'label' => 'As Translator',  'icon' => 'fa-language'],
    'artist'     => ['table' => 'tblSongArtists',     'label' => 'As Artist',      'icon' => 'fa-microphone'],
];

/* tblSongArtists ships in a separate migration (#587); skip it
   gracefully on installs that haven't applied that migration. */
function _personPageArtistsTableExists(\mysqli $db): bool
{
    $r = $db->query(
        "SELECT 1 FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES
          WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE() AND TABLE_NAME = 'tblSongArtists' LIMIT 1"
    );
    $exists = $r && $r->fetch_row() !== null;
    if ($r) $r->close();
    return $exists;
}
if (!_personPageArtistsTableExists($db)) {
    unset($roleTables['artist']);
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

/**
 * iHymns — Shared Admin Link Registry (#460)
 *
 * Single source of truth for every /manage/* destination. Both the
 * top-bar hamburger offcanvas (< lg) and the pinned sidebar (>= lg)
 * iterate this registry, so adding a new admin page means editing
 * one array.
 *
 * Entry shape (positional for tightness — array_map-style consumers
 * can unpack with `[$id, $href, $icon, $label, $ent, $group] = $l;`):
 *
 *   0 id           matches $activePage on the page; drives highlight.
 *   1 href         destination URL.
 *   2 icon         bi-* class (Bootstrap Icons).
 *   3 label        menu text.
 *   4 entitlement  entitlement key required to see this link; null =
 *                  visible to every authenticated admin surface user.
 *   5 group        sidebar section heading; '' = top-level (shown
 *                  above the first group). Groups are rendered in the
 *                  order they first appear in the array.
 */

if (basename($_SERVER['SCRIPT_FILENAME'] ?? '') === basename(__FILE__)) {
    http_response_code(403);
    exit('Access denied.');
}

/* Sidebar group layout (#819). The Content group had grown to 12
   items and dwarfed every other section — split into three more
   meaningful groups (Songs / Catalogue / Access) and consolidated
   Entitlements alongside the other gating concerns under Access.
   The new groups render as collapsible accordion sections in
   admin-sidebar.php and the mobile offcanvas. */
$_adminLinks = [
    /* id                    href                              icon                  label                    entitlement                    group         */
    ['dashboard',            '/manage/',                       'bi-speedometer2',    'Dashboard',             null,                          ''           ],

    /* Songs — per-row content surfaces (#819) */
    ['editor',               '/manage/editor/',                'bi-pencil-square',   'Song Editor',           'edit_songs',                  'Songs'      ],
    ['requests',             '/manage/requests',               'bi-lightbulb',       'Song Requests',         'review_song_requests',        'Songs'      ],
    ['revisions',            '/manage/revisions',              'bi-clock-history',   'Revisions Audit',       'verify_songs',                'Songs'      ],
    ['missing-numbers',      '/manage/missing-numbers',        'bi-binoculars',      'Missing Numbers',       'edit_songs',                  'Songs'      ],
    ['song-link-suggestions','/manage/song-link-suggestions',  'bi-link-45deg',      'Song Link Suggestions', 'edit_songs',                  'Songs'      ],

    /* Catalogue — collection / metadata surfaces (#819) */
    ['songbooks',            '/manage/songbooks',              'bi-book',            'Songbooks',             'manage_songbooks',            'Catalogue'  ],
    ['songbook-series',      '/manage/songbook-series',        'bi-collection',      'Songbook Series',       'manage_songbooks',            'Catalogue'  ],
    ['credit-people',        '/manage/credit-people',          'bi-person-badge',    'Credit People',         'manage_credit_people',        'Catalogue'  ],
    ['languages',            '/manage/languages',              'bi-translate',       'Languages',             'manage_languages',            'Catalogue'  ],
    ['tags',                 '/manage/tags',                   'bi-tags',            'Tags & Themes',         'manage_tags',                 'Catalogue'  ],

    /* Access — gating + permission surfaces (#819) */
    ['restrictions',         '/manage/restrictions',           'bi-shield-lock',     'Content Restrictions',  'manage_content_restrictions', 'Access'     ],
    ['tiers',                '/manage/tiers',                  'bi-stars',           'Access Tiers',          'manage_access_tiers',         'Access'     ],
    ['entitlements',         '/manage/entitlements',           'bi-key',             'Entitlements',          'manage_entitlements',         'Access'     ],

    /* People */
    ['users',                '/manage/users',                  'bi-people',          'Users',                 'view_users',                  'People'     ],
    ['groups',               '/manage/groups',                 'bi-people-fill',     'User Groups',           'manage_user_groups',          'People'     ],
    ['organisations',        '/manage/organisations',          'bi-building',        'Organisations',         'manage_organisations',        'People'     ],
    /* My Organisations (#707) — the entitlement is open to every signed-in
       role; admin-nav.php applies a data-driven hide via
       userHasOwnOrganisation() so non-admins only see this link when they
       hold an admin/owner row in tblOrganisationMembers. */
    ['my-organisations',     '/manage/my-organisations',       'bi-buildings',       'My Organisations',      'manage_own_organisation',     'People'     ],

    /* Operations — reports, maintenance, infrastructure */
    ['analytics',            '/manage/analytics',              'bi-graph-up',        'Analytics',             'view_analytics',              'Operations' ],
    ['ccli-report',          '/manage/ccli-report',            'bi-receipt',         'CCLI Usage Report',     'view_ccli_report',            'Operations' ],
    ['data-health',          '/manage/data-health',            'bi-activity',        'Data Health',           'drop_legacy_tables',          'Operations' ],
    ['activity-log',         '/manage/activity-log',           'bi-journal-text',    'Activity Log',          'view_activity_log',           'Operations' ],
    ['schema-audit',         '/manage/schema-audit',           'bi-clipboard2-data', 'Schema Audit',          'drop_legacy_tables',          'Operations' ],
    ['setup-database',       '/manage/setup-database',         'bi-database-gear',   'Database Setup',        'run_db_install',              'Operations' ],
    ['configuration',        '/manage/configuration',          'bi-sliders',         'Configuration',         'manage_configuration',        'Operations' ],
    ['notifications',        '/manage/notifications',          'bi-bell',            'Notifications',         'manage_notifications',        'Operations' ],

    ['help',                 '/manage/help',                   'bi-life-preserver',  'Help / Guides',         null,                          'Help'       ],
];

/**
 * Entitlement-gated view of the link registry for a given role.
 *
 * `userHasEntitlement()` lives in /includes/entitlements.php and is
 * already required by admin pages via the auth bootstrap; the caller
 * doesn't need to pull it in separately.
 *
 * @param string|null $role The user's role (e.g. 'global_admin').
 * @return array            Links the role is entitled to see.
 */
function visibleAdminLinks(?string $role): array
{
    global $_adminLinks;
    return array_values(array_filter(
        $_adminLinks,
        static fn(array $l): bool => $l[4] === null || userHasEntitlement($l[4], $role)
    ));
}

feat(catalogue): Works — composition grouping with optional ISWC, nesting + external links (#840)

A new top-level catalogue entity that groups multiple tblSongs rows
representing the same underlying composition across different songbooks
/ arrangements / translations. Mirrors MusicBrainz Works ↔ Recordings:
one Work, many member songs.

Schema (idempotent, registered in setup-database):
- tblWorks: Id, ParentWorkId (self-FK, ON DELETE SET NULL — supports
  unlimited nesting like MusicBrainz parent/child works), Iswc (UNIQUE,
  optional, T-NNN.NNN.NNN-C shape), Title, Slug (UNIQUE), Notes.
- tblWorkSongs: composite PK (WorkId, SongId), IsCanonical flag,
  SortOrder, Note. ON DELETE CASCADE on both FKs.
- tblWorkExternalLinks: parallel to the per-entity tables from #833.
- tblExternalLinkTypes.AppliesTo SET widened to include 'work', and
  the seeded type-rows are upserted to flag which apply to Works.

Read paths — SongData:
- _hasWorksSchema() probe (cached on instance)
- _worksMap() bulk attachment by song id; carries Work header + every
  sibling member + Work-level external links per row.
- getWork($slugOrId) → full Work payload for the public page (parent,
  children, members grouped, links categorised).
- _fetchSongRow() now attaches $row['works'].

Public surfaces:
- /work/<slug> via includes/pages/work.php — title + ISWC, parent /
  children navigation, members grouped by songbook, "Find this work
  elsewhere" categorised links.

  belongs to plus "Other versions of this work" siblings.

  + breadcrumb + OG title.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

/**
 * iHymns — Shared <head> library loads for /manage/* (#527)
 *
 * Centralised <link> stylesheet loads for every admin page. Pulls the
 * Bootstrap version + URL + SRI from APP_CONFIG['libraries']['bootstrap']
 * so a version bump propagates to every admin page in one place. The
 * JS counterpart is loaded by admin-footer.php from the same config
 * entry, so CSS and JS versions can never drift again — the cause of
 * the setup-database.php 5.3.6 vs admin-footer.php 5.3.3 mismatch
 * the audit flagged.
 *
 * USAGE
 *   require __DIR__ . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . 'includes' . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . 'head-libs.php';
 * Place inside <head> after <title> (so per-page CSS overrides can
 * still take effect by appending after this require).
 *
 * EXPECTED CALLER STATE
 *   - APP_CONFIG['libraries']['bootstrap'] defined (loaded by
 *     auth.php's bootstrap, available globally on every admin page).
 *
 * Bootstrap-Icons is currently pinned here (no APP_CONFIG entry yet).
 * If a future PR centralises icons into APP_CONFIG['libraries']
 * ['bootstrap_icons'], swap the inline literal for the config lookup
 * the same way bootstrap is treated below.
 */

if (basename($_SERVER['SCRIPT_FILENAME'] ?? '') === basename(__FILE__)) {
    http_response_code(403);
    exit('Access denied.');
}

$_bs = APP_CONFIG['libraries']['bootstrap'] ?? null;
if ($_bs && !empty($_bs['css_cdn'])):
    ?>
    <link rel="stylesheet"
          href="<?= htmlspecialchars((string)$_bs['css_cdn'], ENT_QUOTES) ?>"
          integrity="<?= htmlspecialchars((string)($_bs['css_sri'] ?? ''), ENT_QUOTES) ?>"
          crossorigin="anonymous">
    <?php
endif;
?>
    <link rel="stylesheet"
          href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/font/bootstrap-icons.min.css"
          integrity="sha384-XGjxtQfXaH2tnPFa9x+ruJTuLE3Aa6LhHSWRr1XeTyhezb4abCG4ccI5AkVDxqC+"
          crossorigin="anonymous">
<?php
/* Shared app + admin CSS — paths relative to public_html root.
   `dirname(__DIR__, 2)` from manage/includes/head-libs.php = public_html/. */
$_publicRoot = dirname(__DIR__, 2);
?>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/app.css?v=<?= filemtime($_publicRoot . '/css/app.css') ?>">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/admin.css?v=<?= filemtime($_publicRoot . '/css/admin.css') ?>">

input.body:
### Implemented in branch `claude/add-works-external-links-qKbS4`

Commit: 8f0c72f — `feat(admin): URL auto-detect for external-link provider dropdown (#841)`

**New file:**
- `appWeb/public_html/js/modules/external-link-detect.js` — IIFE exposing `window.iHymnsLinkDetect` (`detectFromUrl`, `slugToOptionValue`, `attachAutoDetect`). 30+ providers covering every slug seeded by `migrate-external-links.php` (#833) plus the `AppliesTo='work'` subset added by `migrate-works.php` (#840).

**Updated files:**
- `appWeb/public_html/manage/includes/head-libs.php` — loads the module on every `/manage/*` page (eager, no `defer`).
- `appWeb/public_html/manage/songbooks.php` — songbook row builder calls `attachAutoDetect` when present.
- `appWeb/public_html/manage/works.php` — Works page wired in the same one-liner pattern.

**Tests:**
- `tests/test-external-link-detect.js` — 44 cases (every provider slug + edge cases). All pass.

**How the manual-choice override works:**
- The provider `<select>` listens for `change`. When it fires with a non-empty value, `data-user-picked="1"` is stamped on the element.
- The URL→provider auto-detector reads that attribute and bails when it's set, so a curator who manually picked "Other" before pasting their URL doesn't get clobbered.
- Programmatic selection (the auto-detector itself) does NOT stamp `data-user-picked`, so users can keep auto-overriding by editing the URL.

**Adding a new provider:** one-line append to the `RULES` array in `external-link-detect.js`. That's the only place — every consumer inherits.

**Known follow-up:** the credit-people edit modal (#838) still uses the legacy free-text `LinkType` field. When that lands on the new schema (per #833 / #838), the same one-line `attachAutoDetect(card)` call will light it up automatically.

refactor(admin): responsive list-view convention — credit-people + songbooks + series + works (#842)

Drives the iPhone-portrait clipping reported on /manage/credit-people:
the Lifespan + Meta + Source columns pushed the table off-screen.
Now they collapse below their breakpoint and stop horizontal-scrolling
the page.

Convention (single CSS rule, opt-in per-page):
- Add the `admin-table-responsive` class to a list <table>.
- Tag every <th> AND its corresponding <td> with one of:
    data-col-priority="primary"    — never hidden
    data-col-priority="secondary"  — hidden ≤ 768px
    data-col-priority="tertiary"   — hidden ≤ 992px

CSS lives in appWeb/public_html/css/admin.css with two media-queries
gated on the class — pages without the class are unaffected, so
rolling it forward to the rest of the admin surfaces is a per-page
change with zero blast radius.

Pages opted in by this commit:
- /manage/credit-people (the screenshot motivator):
    Lifespan, Source → secondary (hide ≤ 768px)
    Meta            → tertiary  (hide ≤ 992px)
    Name, Roles, Total uses, Actions → primary
- /manage/songbooks:
    Drag-handle, Order, Parent, Colour → tertiary
    Official, Languages → secondary
    Abbr, Name, Songs, Actions → primary
- /manage/songbook-series:
    Slug → secondary
    Description → tertiary
    Name, Members, Actions → primary
- /manage/works (#840):
    ISWC → secondary
    Children, Parent → tertiary
    Title, Members, Actions → primary

Per-page rollout for the other admin lists is queued under the
follow-up audit checklist on issue #842.

EOF

# 🔗 External Links & Works

> How iHymns links each hymn / songbook / person out to the rest of the web, and how Works group different versions of the same composition together.

---

## Find this song / songbook / person elsewhere

On every song page, songbook page and person page in iHymns you'll find a **Find this … elsewhere** panel — a categorised list of curated external links pointing at:

- **Official** — the publisher's official website, the songbook's home page
- **Information** — Wikipedia, Wikidata, Hymnary.org, MusicBrainz
- **Read** — Internet Archive scans, Open Library
- **Sheet music** — IMSLP, downloadable PDFs
- **Listen** — Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, Bandcamp, SoundCloud, LibriVox audio recordings
- **Watch** — YouTube performances, Vimeo
- **Purchase** — CCLI SongSelect, publisher stores
- **Authority** — VIAF, OCLC/WorldCat, Library of Congress
- **Social** — Facebook, Instagram, Twitter/X, LinkedIn
- **Other** — anything else a curator has flagged

Each link opens in a new tab. A small ✓ tick beside the link means a curator has personally verified the URL still points at the right resource. The link text usually shows the provider name (e.g. _"Wikipedia"_, _"Spotify"_); a small grey note alongside provides extra context (_"1779 first edition"_, _"sung by King's College Cambridge"_).

Curators add new links via the in-app admin tools — if you spot a link that's gone stale or want to suggest a new one, use **Request a Song** from the menu and mention the URL in the notes.

---

## Works — same composition, multiple sources

A **Work** in iHymns groups together every version of the same underlying composition that appears across multiple songbooks. So _Amazing Grace_ — which exists in dozens of hymnals under slightly different titles, with different arrangements, sometimes translated into other languages — has one **Work** record, and every individual songbook entry is linked back to it.

Visiting `/work/<slug>` shows you:
- The canonical **title** and (where registered) the **ISWC** — the International Standard Musical Work Code
- Every version of the work across the catalogue, grouped by songbook
- The categorised "Find this work elsewhere" panel, just like the song / songbook / person pages
- **Parent / child** works for nested arrangements: an original Work can have child Works for derivative arrangements / translations / choral versions, with unlimited nesting depth (a child can in turn have its own children, and so on).

On any **song** page, if the song belongs to a Work you'll see a "Part of work" panel listing the Work and "Other versions of this work" — a quick way to jump to the same hymn in a different songbook.

### Why ISWC?

The ISWC (`T-NNN.NNN.NNN-C`) is the international identifier for a musical composition, registered with CISAC societies (BMI, ASCAP, PRS, etc.). It's optional in iHymns because not every creative work has one — many traditional / public-domain hymns predate the system, and many newer compositions haven't been registered. When supplied, it gives external integrations (CCLI tooling, MusicBrainz, royalty platforms) a stable cross-reference.

---

## Related

- [Searching Songs](searching-songs.md) — finding a hymn by title, lyrics, or songbook
- [Songbooks](songbooks.md) — navigating the available songbooks

---

Copyright © 2026 MWBM Partners Ltd. All rights reserved.

Key actions

Add
Pre-register a canonical spelling (with optional birth/death info, IPI numbers, external links) so it appears in the editor's autocomplete from day one.
Edit
Update biographical info, links, IPI numbers. Editing a name applies to all songs that cite it.
Rename

Merge
Collapse two registry entries into one. Pick which row survives; all credits on songs are re-pointed to the survivor and the duplicate is deleted.
Delete
