input.new_string:
Works

admin global_admin

A Work groups multiple tblSongs rows that represent the same underlying composition across different songbooks / arrangements / translations — mirrors the MusicBrainz Work ↔ Recording relationship. So Amazing Grace, which appears in dozens of hymnals under slightly different titles, lives as one Work with each songbook entry as a member.

Key actions

Create
Title + slug (auto from title) + optional ISWC + optional parent Work + optional notes. Members are added via the Edit modal once the row exists.
Edit
Add / remove member songs (typeahead over the whole catalogue), mark one as canonical, set sort order, attach external links (the provider dropdown auto-detects from the URL).
Delete
Memberships and external links cascade away with the Work. Child Works (if any) orphan — their ParentWorkId goes to NULL — rather than cascade-delete.

Nesting

Works can be nested without limit: an original Work can have child Works for derivative arrangements, translations, choral versions, etc., each of which can in turn have its own children. Cycles are blocked server-side at update time (no Work can become its own ancestor).

ISWC

The ISWC (T-NNN.NNN.NNN-C) is the international identifier for a musical composition, registered with CISAC societies (BMI, ASCAP, PRS, …). It's optional — many traditional hymns predate the system, and many newer compositions haven't been registered. When supplied, the field shape-validates and canonicalises to the standard format.

Gotcha: The same song can belong to multiple Works (e.g. a medley arrangement that quotes two compositions), but it's rare and usually a misclassification. The list view's "Members" column is the quickest sanity check.

External Links

admin global_admin

Songs, Songbooks, Credit People and Works all support a card-list editor for external links — controlled-vocabulary providers (Wikipedia, Hymnary.org, Spotify, IMSLP, MusicBrainz, etc.) backed by tblExternalLinkTypes. Each link carries an optional Note and a curator-set Verified flag.

URL auto-detect (#841)

Paste a URL into the URL field of any external-link row and the provider dropdown auto-selects the matching registry entry — Wikipedia detects Wikipedia, YouTube detects YouTube, Spotify detects Spotify, etc. The detector respects manual choices: if you pick a provider before pasting, your choice wins.

The detector lives in a single global module — js/modules/external-link-detect.js — loaded on every /manage/* page. Adding a new provider rule is a one-line append; every consumer (Songbook editor, Works editor, Credit People editor as it's added) inherits automatically.

Categories

Links group on the public site under: Official, Information, Read, Sheet music, Listen, Watch, Purchase, Authority, Social, Other. The seeded type registry decides which category each provider belongs to; curators don't pick the category — it's derived from the type.

Mobile admin (responsive list views)

Admin list pages opt into a column-priority responsive convention (#842). Tag the table .admin-table-responsive, then mark each <th> + <td> with data-col-priority="primary", "secondary", or "tertiary". Below 992px tertiary columns hide; below 768px secondary columns hide too. Primary columns are always visible.

Pages currently opted in: Credit People, Songbooks, Songbook Series, Works. The convention is documented in DEV_NOTES.md; rolling it forward to the remaining list pages is a per-page cosmetic change with zero CSS work.

+

Getting started

+

+ The iHymns admin area lives at /manage/ and is the + place where curators, editors, admins, and global admins do + everything that isn't “use the app”: adding songs, + building songbooks, managing user accounts, reviewing requests, + running reports. +

+

+ Every page in the admin area follows the same shape: +

+
    +
  • The top bar always shows the iHymns brand, + your name, and a hamburger menu (on small screens) or the + sidebar (on wide screens) listing every page + you have access to.
    • +
  • The title at the top tells you what page + you're on; below it sits the page's main controls.
    • +
  • Buttons that perform destructive or irreversible + actions (delete, drop, disconnect) always ask for + confirmation. Read the prompt before clicking through.
    • +
  • Pages you don't have permission for are simply not + shown in the menu — there's nothing to click that you + can't actually use.
    • +
+

+ If a page mentions an action that you can't see, you don't have + the entitlement for it. Ask a global admin to grant you the + relevant role or entitlement (see + Roles and + Entitlements below). +

+
+ +
+

Roles & what each one can do

+

iHymns has four account roles, in order of increasing access:

+ +
+
User user
+
+ The default for everyone signing up. No access to + /manage/ at all. Can use the main app, save + favourites, and build setlists. +
+ +
Curator / Editor editor
+
+ Can add and edit songs in the Song Editor, see the + Dashboard, see & act on Song Requests, run the + Missing Numbers report, and manage the Credit People + registry. Cannot see Users, Organisations, or Operations + pages. +
+ +
Admin admin
+
+ Everything an editor can do, plus: manage Users (create, + update, change role up to admin), manage Songbooks, + Organisations, User Groups, Access Tiers, Content + Restrictions, see Analytics, Activity Log, CCLI Report. + Cannot manage Entitlements or run Schema Audit / + Database Setup. +
+ +
Global Admin global_admin
+
+ Everything. Including the safety-critical operations + pages (Database Setup, Schema Audit, Data Health, + Entitlements). Use sparingly — actions on these pages + can affect every user. +
+
+ +

+ Roles are assigned on the Users page. + Role-vs-entitlement mappings can be customised on + Entitlements, but the defaults + match the rules above. +

+
+ +
+

Dashboard

+

+ editor + admin + global_admin +

+

+ The first page you see after signing in. Shows a snapshot of + the library and a quick-link card for every other admin + page you can access. +

+

Key actions

+
    +
  • See library stats (songs, songbooks, setlists, pending requests).
    • +
  • See activity (active users, logins in the last 24 h, song views).
    • +
  • For admins: see a list of the 10 most recently created users.
    • +
  • Customise card layout — drag cards to reorder them, hide cards you never use, save your layout, or (global admins only) save your layout as the site-wide default for new users.
    • +
  • Click any card to jump straight into that admin page.
    • +
+

How it connects

+

+ Stats are live counts from the database — refresh the page to + see the latest. Hidden cards stay hidden until you re-show + them in Settings → Profile. +

+
+ Gotcha: Card customisation is per-user. A + global admin saving their layout as the site-wide default + affects only new users — existing users keep whatever they + already had. +
+
+ Role-gated sections (#641): the dashboard + renders different bottom-of-page cards depending on your + role. Curators / Editors / Admins see a lightweight + Your session card with their role + username. + Global Admins see a richer System Info + card carrying PHP version, database driver and the + connected DB name — useful for triage but not relevant + to curators, so it's deliberately hidden from lower roles. +
+
+ + + +

Song Editor

+

+ editor + admin + global_admin +

+

+ The big one. The Song Editor is where you author and maintain + the catalogue. It loads every song in the library into your + browser, then lets you edit one song or many at once before + saving everything back. +

+

Working with the catalogue

+
    +
  • Filter by songbook, search by title, or + sort by title / number / songbook+number using the + controls above the song list.
    • +
  • Click a song in the list to load it into the tabs on the + right (Metadata, Structure, Credits, Tags, Preview).
    • +
  • Use Multi-select mode for bulk operations + (verify, tag, move to another songbook, export, delete).
    • +
+

The five tabs

+
+
Metadata
+
Title, song number, songbook, CCLI number, Tune Name (e.g. HYFRYDOL), ISWC, language, region.
+
Structure
+
+ The actual lyrics, broken into sections: verses, choruses, bridges, and so on. Drag to reorder; auto-resizing text areas grow as you type. +
+ Verse-1-acts-as-chorus convention (e.g. SDAH-93 "All Things Bright and Beautiful") +
+ Some hymns open with a stanza that's structurally a refrain — the song repeats it after every verse — but the hymnal still numbers it as Verse 1. To set these up: +
    +
  1. Set the first component's Type to Refrain, leaving its number as 1.
    2. +
  2. Click Chorus after each verse in the Arrangement quick-actions. Because the refrain comes before any verse, the arrangement starts and ends each cycle with the refrain — exactly the SDAH-93 playback pattern.
    3. +
+ On the public song page, "Refrain" displays as "Chorus" via the standing alias so existing styling and screen-reader cues stay consistent. +
+
+
+
Credits
+
Writer, composer, arranger, adaptor, translator, copyright holder. Names autocomplete from the Credit People registry so you don't get duplicate spellings.
+
Tags
+
Categorical tags (e.g. Easter, Communion) that drive Browse-by-Theme in the main app and can be used as targets for Content Restrictions.
+
Preview
+
Read-only render of the finished song as users will see it. Always check this before saving.
+
+

Saving, importing, exporting

+
    +
  • Save writes everything to the database. Auto-save runs in the background while you work, but always click Save before navigating away.
    • +
  • Validate runs every song past a quality check (missing required fields, invalid language tags, orphaned references) and lists any problems.
    • +
  • Import from JSON or CSV — small, single-file. For mass onboarding (e.g. a complete new hymnal), see the Bulk Import ZIP section below.
    • +
  • Export the current view as JSON or CSV.
    • +
  • Revisions for the selected song shows a diff of every previous edit and a Restore button.
    • +
+

Bulk Import ZIP (#664 / #676)

+

+ For onboarding an entire songbook at once. Upload a ZIP whose top-level folders match <Hymnal Name> [<ABBR>]/ and whose files match <number> (<ABBR>) - <Title>.txt. The importer creates the songbook on first encounter, then parses + inserts every song. +

+
    +
  • INSERT-only contract: if a songbook or song already exists, it's left untouched — never overwritten. The summary reports created vs. existing counts so you can see what landed.
    • +
  • Live progress widget: the upload completes almost immediately; the actual import runs server-side. A small fixed-position card pinned bottom-right polls the job status, shows a progress bar, and survives navigation between admin pages and the public app. Hard-reload the page mid-import and the widget reattaches via localStorage.
    • +
  • Notification on completion: a row is written to Notifications when the worker finishes, and (if you've granted permission) a native browser notification fires.
    • +
  • Caps: 100 MB upload, 100,000 entries per archive, 5 MiB per uncompressed entry, 500 MiB cumulative uncompressed. These are zip-bomb defences (#682) — far above any real bundle.
    • +
+

Language tagging (IETF BCP 47, #240 / #281 / #681 / #687)

+

+ The Metadata tab's Language field is a composite IETF picker — three sub-fields that compose into a single saved tag: +

+
    +
  • Language (required) — e.g. English (en) or Portuguese (pt).
    • +
  • Script (optional) — only when the script differs from the language default. e.g. Simplified Chinese for Mandarin written in Hans, or Latin for Serbian written Latn instead of the default Cyrl.
    • +
  • Region (optional) — e.g. United Kingdom for British English (en-GB) vs. United States for American English (en-US).
    • +
+

+ The "IETF tag:" line below the picker shows the composed tag live as you type, with a human-readable rendering next to it (e.g. "Spanish (Mexico)" for es-MX). The full ISO 639 / ISO 15924 / ISO 3166-1 vocabulary is loaded from tblLanguages + tblLanguageScripts + tblRegions + tblLanguageVariants — every IANA-registered subtag — so the picker stays in sync with the songbook editor's identical picker. One source of truth across both surfaces. (#681 / #738) +

+

+ The full IANA Language Subtag Registry plus CLDR English display names ship as bundled snapshots in appWeb/.sql/data/. Database Setup → "Refresh BCP 47 reference data" has a live-fetch button if you need to pull the latest IANA / CLDR updates. +

+
+ Gotcha: Closing the tab while there are unsaved changes loses them — auto-save catches most things, but treat Save as the source of truth. +
+
+ Gotcha: A song's ID is set when it's first created and never changes. Renaming the title doesn't rename the ID. Numbering is independent of ID. +
+
+ Gotcha: Deleting a song is permanent. Use Revisions → Restore if you need an old version before you save further edits over it. +
+

Song Requests

+

+ editor + admin + global_admin +

+

+ End users in the main app can submit a song request via the dedicated /request page — reachable from the “Report a missing song or suggest a correction” link at the bottom of every song page, the “Suggest a Missing Song” CTA on /help, and a deep-link from the editor's missing-numbers tool with the songbook + number prefilled. Submissions queue offline and replay automatically when the user is back online; each submission also returns a tracking ID the user can quote when following up. All paths land in this triage list. +

+

Key actions

+
    +
  • Filter by status: Pending, Reviewed, Added, Declined, or All.
    • +
  • Change a request's status inline.
    • +
  • Add an admin note (e.g. "merged with #1234", "no copyright clearance").
    • +
  • If the request was fulfilled by an existing song, paste its ID into Resolved Song ID.
    • +
  • Click Start editing to open the editor pre-loaded with a draft song matching the request, with a back-link to the request.
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: There's no bulk update. Long queues take time. Filter by Pending and work top-down. +
+

Revisions Audit

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ A read-only audit trail of every song edit, ever. Useful for "who changed Amazing Grace last Tuesday?" and as the entry point for restoring an older version. +

+

Key actions

+
    +
  • Filter by user, song ID (partial match works), action (create / edit / restore / delete), and time range (7 / 30 / 90 / 365 days).
    • +
  • Click a row to open that song in the editor; the Revisions modal there shows the diff and lets you Restore.
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: Revisions are immutable. Restore creates a new revision rather than rewriting history, so the trail stays honest. +
+
+ +

Missing Numbers

+

+ editor + admin + global_admin +

+

+ For every songbook, shows the highest number assigned, the count of songs present, and the gaps in numbering. Long gaps are collapsed into ranges (e.g. "#400–#500 · 101 missing") so the page stays readable. +

+

When to use it

+

+ Spot songs that haven't been added yet, find renumbering gaps after deletions, or verify that a freshly-imported songbook is complete. +

+
+ Gotcha: The report is read-only. Use the Song Editor to actually fill the gaps. +
+

Songbooks

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Songbooks are the top-level container — every song lives in exactly one. This page is where you create, name, colour, and order them. +

+

Per-songbook fields

+
+
Abbreviation
Short identifier (e.g. HYM). Unique. Max 10 chars, alphanumeric. This is the natural key referenced by every song.
+
Name
Friendly name (e.g. "Methodist Hymnal").
+
Display order
Numeric sort key — lower numbers appear first in the app.
+
Colour
Hex code (#RRGGBB) used as the songbook tile colour on the home page. Leave blank to let the system auto-pick a tone from the current theme palette (#677) — the result is consistent with the rest of the UI and changes with the user's chosen theme.
+
Official flag
Marks "real" published hymnals vs. user-curated collections / pseudo-songbooks. Used by the home-page filter to separate the two surfaces.
+
Publisher / Publication year / Copyright
Issuing body, year of publication, and the copyright statement. Optional, surface in search and reports.
+
Affiliation
Issuing organisation, drawn from a curated registry (#670). Type to search; new affiliations get added on save. Use this rather than free-text Publisher when the same organisation issues multiple songbooks.
+
Language (IETF BCP 47)
The songbook's primary language as a composite IETF tag (#673 / #681) — same picker as the song editor, with three sub-fields: Language (required), Script (optional — only when the script differs from the language default), and Region (optional — e.g. en-GB vs en-US). Leave blank for multi-lingual collections.
+
Online links — Official website / Internet Archive / Wikipedia (#672)
Free-text URLs. Used as outbound references on the songbook detail page so users can verify the source.
+
Authority identifiers — WikiData ID, OCLC, OCN, LCP, ISBN, ARK, ISNI, VIAF, LCCN, LC Class (#672)
Standard cataloguing identifiers from major library and authority systems. All optional. Useful for cross-referencing and de-duplicating against external catalogues.
+
+

Renaming an abbreviation

+

+ Abbreviations are the natural key, so renaming is opt-in: you must tick the "Also rename song references" checkbox to cascade the rename to every song that uses it. Without that checkbox, songs keep the old abbreviation and orphan from the renamed songbook. +

+

Colour picker

+

+ The Colour field accepts a 7-char #RRGGBB hex value (#715). The browser-native colour picker writes the canonical lower-case hex back into the text field when you confirm a swatch — handy if you want to copy the value into another tool. Leave the field blank to let the system auto-pick a tone the catalogue isn't already using; the next save fills the field in for you. +

+

Auto-colour bulk action

+

+ Two destructive-but-recoverable buttons live at the top of the songbook list (#716): +

+
+
Auto-fill blank colours
+
Walks every songbook; rows with NULL or non-#RRGGBB colours get a fresh palette pick. Existing valid hex values are left alone — idempotent, safe to re-run.
+
Reassign every colour
+
Overwrites every Colour value, regardless of whether it was set already. Gated by typing the literal phrase REASSIGN ALL — defence-in-depth so a stray click never re-themes the whole catalogue.
+
+

Cascade delete

+

+ The default Delete refuses if any song still references the songbook abbreviation. Admin / global_admin can use Cascade delete instead, which removes the songbook AND every song in it AND every credit / tag / chord / translation that referenced those songs (#706). Server-side typed-confirmation gate: the curator must type the songbook abbreviation exactly. The FK chain handles the rest atomically. +

+
+ Gotcha: Deleting a songbook does not delete its songs unless you use Cascade delete. The standard UI refuses if any song still references its abbreviation; reassign or delete those songs first. +
+
+ Tip: The home-page tile grid (#678) shows official hymnals first, with a language filter (#679 / #736 v2) that lets users pick which languages to show across both songbook tiles AND individual song listings (search, popular, recently-viewed). Multi-select is supported; signed-in users get the choice persisted to their account and synced across devices. The Misc pseudo-songbook is always pinned to the bottom of the grid (#717) regardless of DisplayOrder — it's a catch-all and should never out-rank a curated hymnal. Songbooks AND songs without a Language field always show, regardless of the filter — useful for catch-all collections. +
+
+ +
+

Credit People

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ A registry of every named person credited on a song — writers, composers, arrangers, adaptors, translators. Lets you fix the “J. Newton vs John Newton” problem in one place instead of in every song that mentions them. +

+

Key actions

+
+
Add
Pre-register a canonical spelling (with optional birth/death info, IPI numbers, external links) so it appears in the editor's autocomplete from day one.
+
Edit
Update biographical info, links, IPI numbers. Editing a name applies to all songs that cite it.
+
Rename
Change the canonical name and cascade the change atomically across every song that cites it.
+
Merge
Collapse two registry entries into one. Pick which row survives; all credits on songs are re-pointed to the survivor and the duplicate is deleted.
+
Delete
Remove from the registry. Refuses by default if any song still cites them; force-delete is available behind a confirmation.
+
View Songs
Modal showing every song that cites a person, grouped by role (writer, composer, …).
+
+
+ Gotcha: Rename and Merge are atomic — either every credit on every song updates, or none does. Half-finished states are not possible. +
+
+ +
+

Works

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ A Work groups multiple tblSongs rows that represent the same underlying composition across different songbooks / arrangements / translations — mirrors the MusicBrainz Work ↔ Recording relationship. So Amazing Grace, which appears in dozens of hymnals under slightly different titles, lives as one Work with each songbook entry as a member. +

+

Key actions

+
+
Create
Title + slug (auto from title) + optional ISWC + optional parent Work + optional notes. Members are added via the Edit modal once the row exists.
+
Edit
Add / remove member songs (typeahead over the whole catalogue), mark one as canonical, set sort order, attach external links (the provider dropdown auto-detects from the URL).
+
Delete
Memberships and external links cascade away with the Work. Child Works (if any) orphan — their ParentWorkId goes to NULL — rather than cascade-delete.
+
+

Nesting

+

+ Works can be nested without limit: an original Work can have child Works for derivative arrangements, translations, choral versions, etc., each of which can in turn have its own children. Cycles are blocked server-side at update time (no Work can become its own ancestor). +

+

ISWC

+

+ The ISWC (T-NNN.NNN.NNN-C) is the international identifier for a musical composition, registered with CISAC societies (BMI, ASCAP, PRS, …). It's optional — many traditional hymns predate the system, and many newer compositions haven't been registered. When supplied, the field shape-validates and canonicalises to the standard format. +

+
+ Gotcha: The same song can belong to multiple Works (e.g. a medley arrangement that quotes two compositions), but it's rare and usually a misclassification. The list view's "Members" column is the quickest sanity check. +
+
+ +
+

External Links

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Songs, Songbooks, Credit People and Works all support a card-list editor for external links — controlled-vocabulary providers (Wikipedia, Hymnary.org, Spotify, IMSLP, MusicBrainz, etc.) backed by tblExternalLinkTypes. Each link carries an optional Note and a curator-set Verified flag. +

+

URL auto-detect (#841)

+

+ Paste a URL into the URL field of any external-link row and the provider dropdown auto-selects the matching registry entry — Wikipedia detects Wikipedia, YouTube detects YouTube, Spotify detects Spotify, etc. The detector respects manual choices: if you pick a provider before pasting, your choice wins. +

+

+ The detector lives in a single global module — js/modules/external-link-detect.js — loaded on every /manage/* page. Adding a new provider rule is a one-line append; every consumer (Songbook editor, Works editor, Credit People editor as it's added) inherits automatically. +

+

Categories

+

Links group on the public site under: Official, Information, Read, Sheet music, Listen, Watch, Purchase, Authority, Social, Other. The seeded type registry decides which category each provider belongs to; curators don't pick the category — it's derived from the type.

+
+ +
+

Mobile admin (responsive list views)

+

+ Admin list pages opt into a column-priority responsive convention (#842). Tag the table .admin-table-responsive, then mark each <th> + <td> with data-col-priority="primary", "secondary", or "tertiary". Below 992px tertiary columns hide; below 768px secondary columns hide too. Primary columns are always visible. +

+

+ Pages currently opted in: Credit People, Songbooks, Songbook Series, Works. The convention is documented in DEV_NOTES.md; rolling it forward to the remaining list pages is a per-page cosmetic change with zero CSS work. +

+

Content Restrictions

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Rule-based access control. Each rule says "for this thing, on this platform / for this user / when this licence is or isn't held, allow or deny." +

+

Anatomy of a rule

+
+
Entity
What's being restricted: a single song, an entire songbook, or a feature like audio playback.
+
Restriction type
How: block by platform / block by user / block by org / require a licence / require an org membership.
+
Target
The thing on the other side of the rule: a platform name, user ID, org ID, or licence type.
+
Effect
Allow or Deny when this rule fires.
+
Priority (0–1000)
Higher beats lower. At equal priority, Deny beats Allow.
+
Reason
Free-text note. Strongly recommended — future-you will thank present-you.
+
+

Common patterns

+
    +
  • Hide a song from a specific platform — block_platform with target = platform name.
    • +
  • Restrict copyrighted songs to CCLI holders — require_licence with target = ccli.
    • +
  • Allow only one user to see a draft song — block_user for everyone (low priority) plus an Allow rule (high priority) for that user.
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: Rules are evaluated at request time. Changes take effect on the next page load — but data already cached on a user's device may lag a few minutes. +
+
+ +
+

Access Tiers

+

+ global_admin +

+

+ Tiers are bundles of capabilities (view lyrics, view copyrighted lyrics, play audio, download MIDI, download PDF, save offline, requires CCLI). Every user is assigned one tier, which controls what UI controls they see in the main app. +

+

Default tiers (seeded at install)

+
    +
  • public — lyrics only, public-domain only.
    • +
  • free — lyrics, no audio, no copyrighted content.
    • +
  • ccli — lyrics + copyrighted, but only if the user's organisation has a CCLI licence number.
    • +
  • premium — everything except offline.
    • +
  • pro — everything.
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: A tier's machine name is set on creation and never changes. To “rename” a tier, create a new one, reassign users to it, then delete the old one. +
+
+ + + +
+

Users

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Manage every user account: create accounts, assign roles, deactivate, reset passwords, change tiers. +

+

Key actions

+
    +
  • Create — username (min 3 chars, lowercase letters / digits / dot / hyphen / underscore), password REDACTED 8 chars), display name, role, tier.
    • +
  • Edit profile — display name, email, tier.
    • +
  • Change role — admins can only assign roles at or below their own; only a global admin can promote someone to admin or global admin.
    • +
  • Activate / Deactivate — deactivated users cannot sign in.
    • +
  • Reset password — sets a new password REDACTED (the user is not auto-signed-out from existing sessions).
    • +
  • Delete — permanent. Their setlists, song revisions, and activity entries remain (linked by user ID) for audit reasons.
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: You cannot deactivate your own account. +
+
+ Gotcha: Username is set on creation and is immutable. Display name can be changed any time. +
+

User Groups

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Logical buckets of users for shared release-channel access (Alpha / Beta / RC / RTW). Useful for “who sees pre-release content?” without managing flags per-user. +

+

Key actions

+
    +
  • Create a group with a name, description, and four channel flags.
    • +
  • Two-pane membership editor: drag users between “Available” and “In group.”
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: One group per user. Re-assigning moves them; there's no “in two groups at once.” +
+
+ Role vs Group (#642): these names sound similar but they're independent concepts. +
    +
  • User Role (Curator / Admin / Global Admin) controls which Manage pages a user can access. The four roles are hard-coded today; new roles need a code change.
    • +
  • User Group controls which release channel a user sees on the public site (Alpha / Beta / RC / RTW). Group membership is freely admin-managed via this page.
    • +
+ Don't expect adding a User Group to grant Manage access — for that, change the user's Role from User Management. Issue #642 tracks the rationalisation. +

Organisations

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Churches, denominations, schools. Group users together and attach a single licence (CCLI / iHymns Pro / iHymns Basic) to that group instead of to each user. +

+

Per-org fields

+
+
Slug
URL-safe identifier (auto-derived from name; you can override). Unique.
+
Parent org
Optional; lets you build a denomination → diocese → church chain. Licences inherit downward.
+
Licence type / number
none, ihymns_basic, ihymns_pro, or ccli. CCLI requires a licence number for audit.
+
Active flag
Inactive orgs are kept in the database but their licence stops counting toward members.
+
+

Membership

+

Two-pane picker, same shape as User Groups. Each member also gets a sub-role: member (no extra perms), admin (can manage other members), or owner (full control of the org).

+
+ Gotcha: An org cannot be its own parent (and we block circular chains in general). +
+
+ +
+

My Organisations

+

+ org admin + org owner + admin + global_admin +

+

+ The org-admin surface (#707, #726). Visible to anyone who holds an admin or owner row in tblOrganisationMembers for at least one organisation — they don't need system-admin role to see this page. System admins see it too, scoped to every org. +

+

What it does

+
    +
  • Lists every organisation the current user can manage.
    • +
  • For each, shows the member roster with role badges and the licence rows on file.
    • +
  • Inline forms for the six edit actions described below — you don't need /manage/organisations for routine org-admin work.
    • +
+

Member actions

+
+
Add member
Free-text identifier — type a username OR an email, the server resolves to a tblUsers.Id. New member rows pick a sub-role (member / admin / owner).
+
Change member role
Inline picker per row.
+
Remove member
You can't remove yourself unless you're also a system admin — prevents accidental org lock-out. Ask a co-admin.
+
+

Licence actions

+
+
Add licence
Per-row licence types: ccli, mrl, ihymns_basic, ihymns_pro, custom. INSERT-on-conflict-UPDATE so re-adding the same type updates number / expiry / notes in place.
+
Change licence
Edit number, expiry date, active flag, notes. Type is immutable on a row — to switch types, remove and re-add.
+
Remove licence
Drops the row. Belt-and-braces ownership check on the server.
+
+

Row-level gate

+

+ Every action runs userCanActOnOrg($userId, $orgId) server-side before any mutation, regardless of whether the call came from the form or a crafted POST. A licence_id from one org can never be edited via an org_id you happen to admin elsewhere. +

+
+ Gotcha: System admins (admin / global_admin) bypass the row-level gate by default. The audit log records the action under org_admin.<verb> regardless, so the timeline reads as one surface. +
+
+ +
+

Entitlements

+

+ global_admin +

+

+ The fine-grained permission map. Every admin action is gated by an entitlement (e.g. edit_songs, verify_songs, manage_songbooks). This page lets you change which roles hold which entitlements, overriding the hard-coded defaults. +

+

When to use it

+
    +
  • Promote a single privilege to a role that doesn't normally have it (e.g. let editors run the CCLI report).
    • +
  • Demote a privilege you want to lock down (e.g. take delete_songs away from admins, leave it with global admins only).
    • +
  • Reset to defaults if you've gone too far — the “Reset” button restores the hard-coded baseline.
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: This is a nuclear tool. A bad change is global, immediate, and visible to everyone on next page load. Make small changes and verify before moving on. +
+
+ Gotcha: The page enforces one safety guard: manage_entitlements itself can never be removed from global_admin, so you can't lock yourself out of the page that re-grants access. +
+
+ + + +
+

Analytics

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Read-only dashboard of usage metrics: top songs, top songbooks, search queries, login counts, user growth. Pick a window (7 / 30 / 90 days) and read off the panels. +

+

Exporting

+

Each panel has a CSV download button that respects the current window.

+
+ Gotcha: Search-query tracking is optional. If your install doesn't log search terms, that panel will be empty. (No personally identifying information is logged either way.) +
+
+ +
+

CCLI Usage Report

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Compliance report for CCLI licensees. Pick a date range and get a sortable table of every CCLI-numbered song with its view count and copyright info, ready to upload to your CCLI reporting portal. +

+

Tips

+
    +
  • The CSV export is the column shape your CCLI portal expects (title, CCLI number, copyright, count).
    • +
  • Tick “Show all” to also include songs without a CCLI number assigned — useful for spotting gaps in the metadata.
    • +
  • The view-count is per occurrence: a user opening the same song twice counts as two views.
    • +
+
+ +
+

Data Health

+

+ global_admin +

+

+ Confirms that MySQL is the authoritative source for every kind of data, and lets you safely disconnect the legacy fallbacks (the original songs.json, the SQLite user database, the file-system setlist share directory) so the app stops checking them. +

+

Workflow

+
    +
  1. Read the row counts at the top to confirm MySQL has the data you expect.
    2. +
  2. Click Disconnect next to a fallback. The file is renamed to .disabled, not deleted — you can restore it manually if needed.
    3. +
  3. Reload the main app to confirm everything still works without the fallback.
    4. +
+
+ Gotcha: One-way lever. There's no “Reconnect” button — restoring a fallback means renaming the .disabled file back by hand on the server. +
+
+ +
+

Activity Log

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Every action that mutates data (creates, edits, deletes, sign-ins, sign-outs, role changes, etc.) writes a row here. Searchable, filterable, exportable. +

+

Filters

+
    +
  • User — username or email substring.
    • +
  • Action / Result / Entity type — pick from a list.
    • +
  • Entity ID — the thing that was acted on.
    • +
  • Request ID — trace every row that came from a single browser request (useful when debugging a multi-step action).
    • +
  • Time window — 1 / 7 / 30 / 90 / 365 days.
    • +
  • Free text — matches the action name and entity ID. Use the specific filters for everything else.
    • +
+

CSV export

+

Respects every active filter; capped at 10 000 rows per download.

+

Error capture (#695)

+

+ Server-side exceptions raised by admin POST handlers (the “Database error — check server logs” banner) are mirrored into the activity log with Result='error' and the exception message + class in the Details column. The viewer's Result = error filter is a one-click triage list — you no longer need SSH to see why a save failed. +

+

+ Verb prefix convention: web admin writes <entity>.<verb> (e.g. songbook.create, org.member_add); the public-API surfaces use api.admin.<entity>.<verb> (e.g. api.admin.songbook.create) so timeline readers can tell which surface drove the change. +

+
+ Gotcha: Rows are immutable. There's no edit, no delete — that's the whole point of an audit log. +
+
+ +
+

Schema Audit

+

+ global_admin +

+

+ Diagnostic page that compares three things: the schema your code expects (schema.sql), the schema your live database actually has, and the migration scripts that bridge the two. Surfaces drift before it bites. +

+

Status meanings

+
+
OK
In code and in DB. Nothing to do.
+
Missing (amber)
In code, not in DB, but a migration covers it. Run that migration on Database Setup.
+
Uncovered (red)
In code, not in DB, and no migration covers it. This is a real bug — an existing install will never get this column. File an issue and write a migration.
+
Orphan
In DB, not in code. Almost always informational — a column you removed from schema.sql is still around in the database. Safe to leave alone.
+
+
+ Gotcha: Schema Audit is read-only. It tells you what's wrong; it never runs ALTER statements itself. +
+
+ +
+

Database Setup

+

+ global_admin +

+

+ The most powerful page in the admin area. Configures the database connection, installs the schema, runs migrations, takes backups, restores from backup. Treat with respect. +

+

Setup workflow on a new install

+
    +
  1. Credentials — fill in host, port, database name, username, password, table prefix. Click Test connection; only save once it goes green.
    2. +
  2. Install schema — creates every table from schema.sql. Idempotent — re-running is safe.
    3. +
  3. Migrate songs JSON — one-time import of data/songs.json into the database.
    4. +
  4. Migrate users / setlists — one-time import from the legacy SQLite + JSON setlist share dir.
    5. +
  5. Run remaining migrations (Account Sync, Songbook Metadata, Credit Fields, Credit People, User Features Catch-up, Activity Log Expand) in the order they appear on the dashboard. Each is idempotent.
    6. +
+

Setup workflow on an existing install

+

+ Re-run Install schema if anything changed in schema.sql (it's safe), then run only the migrations that Schema Audit flagged as missing. Migrations are idempotent — running one that's already been applied just reports “[skip]” for everything. +

+

Apply all pending migrations (#577)

+

+ The Apply all pending migrations button runs every migrate-*.php script in deployment order. Each script is already idempotent, so re-running the bulk action after some have been applied is safe — they no-op individually. +

+

+ If a migration fails mid-run, the dashboard captures the first-failing step and surfaces it in a prominent banner above the (sometimes long, scrollable) output panel (#720), so you don't miss the FAILED line in the noise. Fix the underlying issue and re-run — the steps that succeeded earlier no-op the second time. +

+

Backups

+
    +
  • Backup downloads a SQL dump of the entire database. Keep at least one before running unfamiliar migrations.
    • +
  • Restore uploads a previously downloaded dump and replays it — completely overwrites the current database. Read the warning before you click.
    • +
+

Cleanup

+

Deletes expired API tokens, old login attempts (>30 days), expired email-login codes, etc. Safe to run any time.

+
+ Gotcha: Migrations are not reversible. Always take a backup before running any migration on production. +
+
+ Gotcha: The table prefix is fixed at install time and cannot be changed afterwards. Pick once, live with it. +
+
+ Gotcha: Restore overwrites everything. There is no “merge” option. +
+
+ +
+

Native API surface

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Every admin verb on this site is also reachable via the public REST API at /api.php?action=<verb> (#719). Native clients (Apple, Android, FireOS) and tooling clients (CI, monitoring, dashboards) can drive the same surfaces the web admin uses without a webview or a separate auth flow. +

+

Auth

+

+ Bearer-token auth via the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Tokens are issued by the existing email-magic-link or password REDACTED flows and live on tblApiTokens. POSTs also need X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest as a CSRF defence (#293). Same role gates as the web admin — admin / global_admin for system-wide write verbs, plus the row-level userCanActOnOrg() check for org-admin endpoints. +

+

What's covered

+
    +
  • Songbooks — create / update / delete / cascade-delete / reorder / auto-colour fill / auto-colour reassign (PR 2a).
    • +
  • Users + Groups + Tiers — full CRUD plus role / activate / password-reset / member-add-remove (PR 2b).
    • +
  • Organisations + My Organisations — system-admin updates plus the six org-admin verbs from this surface (PR 2c).
    • +
  • Credit People — add / update / rename / merge / delete with the same cascade and confirmation gates (PR 2d).
    • +
  • Analytics + Diagnostics — top searches, data health snapshot, schema-audit report, per-migration applied/partial/pending status (PR 2d).
    • +
  • Editor — load / save / save_song / bulk_tag / list_revisions / restore_revision / get_translations / add_translation / remove_translation / song_tags / tag_search / credit_search / user_search / org_search / bulk_import_zip / bulk_import_status (PR 3 docs).
    • +
+

OpenAPI spec

+

+ Every endpoint is documented in /api-docs.yaml as a single OpenAPI 3.0 file. Swagger UI / Stoplight / Redoc all render it cleanly. The spec is the source of truth for the request / response shapes — the web admin uses the helpers underneath, the native clients hit the documented endpoints, both stay in sync because the validators live in shared includes/ files. +

+

Activity-log surface prefix

+

+ API-driven changes write under api.admin.<entity>.<verb> (e.g. api.admin.songbook.create, api.org_admin.licence_change). The Activity Log viewer can show both surfaces side-by-side; the prefix tells you which. +

+
+ Gotcha: Status codes follow REST: 400 (validation), 401, 403 (role gate or row-level refusal), 404, 405 (wrong method), 409 (duplicate key), 422 (cannot delete because dependents exist). Native UIs can render the right toast without parsing the error string. +
+
+ + + +
+

Troubleshooting & FAQs

+ +

“A page that should be in the menu isn't there.”

+

+ You don't have the entitlement for it. The menu only shows pages + you can use. Ask a global admin to grant you the role or + entitlement you need (see Entitlements). +

+ +

“I clicked Save in the editor but my changes aren't there after a refresh.”

+

+ Two common causes: +

+
    +
  • The save was rejected by validation. Look for an error toast at the top right of the editor.
    • +
  • You're editing on one device and viewing on another, with one of them having a service-worker cache that hasn't refreshed yet. A hard refresh (Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-R) typically clears it.
    • +
+ +

“I deleted a song by mistake.”

+

+ Open Revisions Audit, find the song's last edit before the delete, click through to the editor, and use Revisions → Restore. Revisions are kept indefinitely so older deletes are still recoverable. +

+ +

“The dashboard / a /manage page is blank.”

+

+ This is rare. Try a hard refresh first. If still blank, append ?_debug=1&_dev=1 to the URL on Alpha or Beta — the server will print any underlying PHP fatal at the bottom of the response. Capture that and pass it to a developer. +

+ +

“A user reports the main app is showing the wrong songs / locking out features.”

+

+ Check three places, in order: +

+
    +
  1. Their access tier on Users — controls capability gating.
    2. +
  2. Their organisation membership — org licence bubbles down to members.
    3. +
  3. Content Restrictions — rules can block or require things on a per-user / per-org / per-platform basis.
    4. +
+ +

“Two songs / two people / two anything look like duplicates.”

+

+ For people, use Credit People → Merge. For songs, the editor doesn't have a merge tool yet — the safest path is to copy any unique data from one into the other, then delete the duplicate. +

+ +

“Activity Log shows an action I don't recognise. What is it?”

+

+ Activity Log entries follow a verb_noun shape (e.g. create_user, edit_song, delete_organisation_member). The Entity type column tells you what was acted on, the Entity ID is its primary key. Click around — most actions can be reverse-engineered from the noun. +

+ +

“Where do I report a bug or request a feature?”

+

+ Either through your usual channel into the iHymns team, or by e-mail to your iHymns administrator. If you have GitHub access, file an issue at the project repository. +

+
+ +
+
+
+ + + +

---

## 📋 Table of Contents

- [Deployment Keys & Secrets](#-deployment-keys--secrets)
- [Song Data Format](#-song-data-format)

## 🔑 Deployment Keys & Secrets

All automated deployment is handled via GitHub Actions. Secrets and variables are configured in **GitHub Repo Settings → Secrets and Variables → Actions**.

### 🌐 Web/PWA — SFTP Deployment

The web app deploys via SFTP using `lftp` (mirroring the phpWhoIs pattern).

| Secret/Variable | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SFTP_HOST` | ✅ Secret | SFTP server hostname (e.g., `ftp.ihymns.app` or `ihymns.app`) |
| `SFTP_PORT` | ❌ Secret | SFTP port number. Defaults to `22` if empty/blank/non-numeric |
| `SFTP_USER` | ✅ Secret | SFTP username for authentication |
| `SFTP_KEY` | ⭐ Secret | SSH private key for key-based auth (preferred over password) |
| `SFTP_PASSWORD` | ⭐ Secret | SFTP password REDACTED if `SFTP_KEY` is not set) |
| `SFTP_LIVE_PATH` | ✅ Secret | Remote path for production (e.g., `/home/user/ihymns.app/public_html/`) |
| `SFTP_BETA_PATH` | ✅ Secret | Remote path for beta (e.g., `/home/user/beta.ihymns.app/public_html/`) |
| `SFTP_DEV_PATH` | ❌ Secret | Remote path for alpha/dev (e.g., `/home/user/dev.ihymns.app/public_html/`) |
| `SFTP_PRIVATE_PATH` | ❌ Secret | Remote path for private_html (e.g., `/home/user/admin.ihymns.app/`) — song editor, admin tools |
| `SFTP_ENABLED` | ✅ Variable | Set to `true` to enable SFTP deployment (kill switch). **Must be a Variable, not a Secret.** |

> ⭐ Either `SFTP_KEY` or `SFTP_PASSWORD` is required. SSH key auth is preferred.

## 🔗 External Links System (#833) and Auto-Detect Module (#841)

### Schema

External links live in three sibling per-entity tables, all pointing
back at one controlled-vocabulary registry:

| Table | Owns the relationship for |
| --- | --- |
| `tblExternalLinkTypes` | The seeded provider registry (~37 types covering Wikipedia, Hymnary.org, MusicBrainz, IMSLP, Spotify, YouTube, etc.) — see `migrate-external-links.php` |
| `tblSongbookExternalLinks` | `tblSongbooks` ↔ link types |
| `tblSongExternalLinks` | `tblSongs` ↔ link types |
| `tblCreditPersonExternalLinks` | `tblCreditPeople` ↔ link types |
| `tblWorkExternalLinks` | `tblWorks` ↔ link types (#840) |

`tblExternalLinkTypes.AppliesTo` is a `SET('song','songbook','person','work')`
that decides which entity types each provider applies to. The Works
migration (`migrate-works.php`) widens this set + seeds the `'work'`
flag on the appropriate provider rows.

Per-entity rows carry: `Url` (≤ 2048 chars), `Note`, `SortOrder`,
`Verified`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`. FK on the entity is
`ON DELETE CASCADE`; FK on the link type is `ON DELETE RESTRICT`
(so the registry can't be accidentally trimmed under live data).

### Read path

`SongData::_externalLinksMap($entityType, $keys)` is the generic
helper. Probe-gated on the relevant `tblXxxExternalLinks` table;
joins `tblExternalLinkTypes` and excludes rows where `IsActive = 0`
(soft delete). Returns a map keyed by Abbreviation / SongId /
CreditPersonId / WorkId.

### URL → Provider auto-detect (#841)

Single source of truth in `appWeb/public_html/js/modules/external-link-detect.js`,
exposed on `window.iHymnsLinkDetect`:

- `detectFromUrl(url)` → slug or `null`
- `slugToOptionValue(selectEl, slug)` → numeric option value or `''`
- `attachAutoDetect(rowEl, opts)` → teardown function

Loaded on every `/manage/*` page by `manage/includes/head-libs.php`,
so each per-page row builder calls
`window.iHymnsLinkDetect.attachAutoDetect(card)` and inherits the
behaviour without an extra script tag.

**Adding a new provider:** append to the `RULES` array in the module.
That's the only place — every consumer inherits.

**Manual-choice override:** `data-user-picked="1"` on the `<select>`
once the user changes it explicitly. The detector reads that attr
and bails when set.

---

## 🎼 Works (#840) — composition grouping

`tblWorks` groups multiple `tblSongs` rows representing the same
composition across different songbooks / arrangements / translations.
Mirrors the MusicBrainz Work ↔ Recording relationship.

### Schema

```
tblWorks
  Id               PK
  ParentWorkId     self-FK, ON DELETE SET NULL → unlimited nesting
  Iswc             CHAR(15), UNIQUE, optional
  Title            VARCHAR(255)
  Slug             VARCHAR(80), UNIQUE
  Notes            TEXT
  CreatedAt / UpdatedAt

tblWorkSongs
  WorkId, SongId   composite PK
  IsCanonical      flag (zero or one per Work, by convention)
  SortOrder
  Note

tblWorkExternalLinks
  same shape as the per-entity link tables (see above).
```

### Read path

returns the full Work payload for the public `/work/<slug>` page.

## 🔗 External Links System (#833) and Auto-Detect Module (#841)

### Schema

External links live in a controlled-vocabulary registry plus per-entity
sibling tables:

| Table | Owns the relationship for |
| --- | --- |
| `tblExternalLinkTypes` | The seeded provider registry (~37 types: Wikipedia, Hymnary.org, MusicBrainz, IMSLP, Spotify, YouTube, …) — see `migrate-external-links.php` |
| `tblSongbookExternalLinks` | `tblSongbooks` ↔ link types |
| `tblSongExternalLinks` | `tblSongs` ↔ link types |
| `tblCreditPersonExternalLinks` | `tblCreditPeople` ↔ link types |
| `tblWorkExternalLinks` | `tblWorks` ↔ link types (#840) |

`tblExternalLinkTypes.AppliesTo` is a `SET('song','songbook','person','work')`
that decides which entity types each provider applies to. The Works
migration (`migrate-works.php`) widens this set + seeds the `'work'`
flag on the appropriate provider rows.

Per-entity rows carry: `Url` (≤ 2048 chars), `Note`, `SortOrder`,
`Verified`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`. FK on the entity is
`ON DELETE CASCADE`; FK on the link type is `ON DELETE RESTRICT`
(so the registry can't be accidentally trimmed under live data).

### Read path

`SongData::_externalLinksMap($entityType, $keys)` is the generic
helper. Probe-gated on the relevant `tblXxxExternalLinks` table;
joins `tblExternalLinkTypes` and excludes rows where `IsActive = 0`
(soft delete). Returns a map keyed by Abbreviation / SongId /
CreditPersonId.

### URL → Provider auto-detect (#841)

Single source of truth in
`appWeb/public_html/js/modules/external-link-detect.js`, exposed on
`window.iHymnsLinkDetect`:

- `detectFromUrl(url)` → slug or `null`
- `slugToOptionValue(selectEl, slug)` → numeric option value or `''`
- `attachAutoDetect(rowEl, opts)` → teardown function

Loaded on every `/manage/*` page by `manage/includes/head-libs.php`,
so each per-page row builder calls
`window.iHymnsLinkDetect.attachAutoDetect(card)` and inherits the
behaviour without an extra script tag.

**Adding a new provider:** append a rule to the `RULES` array in
the module. That's the only place — every consumer inherits.

**Manual-choice override:** `data-user-picked="1"` is stamped on the
`<select>` once the user changes it explicitly. The detector reads
that attr and bails when set.

+## MySQL Database Setup (v0.10.0+)
+
+Starting with v0.10.0, iHymns uses MySQL as the primary data store, with JSON fallback for environments without a database. MySQL provides full-text search indexing, concurrent write safety, user accounts, and features like popular songs, song tags, and translation linking.
+
+### Prerequisites
+
+- **MySQL 5.7+** or **MariaDB 10.3+** with InnoDB support
+- **PHP 8.1+** with the `mysqli` extension enabled
+- A MySQL database created for iHymns:
+  ```sql
+  CREATE DATABASE ihymns CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
+  ```
+
+### Step-by-Step Installation
+
+#### Step 1: Run the Interactive Installer
+
+```bash
+php appWeb/.sql/install.php
+```
+
+The wizard prompts for:
+
+| Prompt | Default | Description |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| MySQL Host | `127.0.0.1` | Server hostname or IP |
+| MySQL Port | `3306` | Server port |
+| Database Name | `ihymns` | Must already exist |
+| Username | `ihymns_user` | MySQL user with full privileges on the DB |
+| Password | _(none)_ | Hidden input on supported terminals |
+| Table Prefix | _(none)_ | Optional prefix (e.g., `ih_`) for shared databases |
+
+The installer will:
+
+1. Test the connection before writing anything
+2. Write credentials to `appWeb/.auth/db_credentials.php` (permissions `0600`)
+3. Create all 30+ tables from `schema.sql` (idempotent — safe to re-run)
+4. Seed default data: user groups, 14 languages, 5 access tiers, app settings
+
+> **Manual setup:** Copy `appWeb/.auth/db_credentials.example.php` to `db_credentials.php`, edit it, then re-run the installer.
+
+#### Step 2: Migrate Song Data from JSON
+
+```bash
+php appWeb/.sql/migrate-json.php
+```
+
+This imports all songs from `data/songs.json` into MySQL:
+- Clears existing song data and re-imports (transaction-wrapped)
+- Populates: songbooks, songs, writers, composers, components
+- Imports translation links from `songs[].translations` array
+- Builds `LyricsText` column for MySQL FULLTEXT search
+
+> Specify a custom path: `php appWeb/.sql/migrate-json.php --json=/path/to/songs.json`
+
+#### Step 3: Create Initial Admin User
+
+Navigate to `/manage/setup` in the browser. The first account becomes the **Global Admin**.
+
+#### Step 4: Verify Installation
+
+Navigate to `/manage/setup-database.php` to see:
+- Database connection status
+- Table row counts
+- Run additional migrations (users, cleanup, backup)
+
+#### Web-Based Setup (No CLI Required)
+
+For shared hosting without SSH:
+
+1. Copy `appWeb/.auth/db_credentials.example.php` to `db_credentials.php` and edit
+2. Navigate to `/manage/setup-database.php`
+3. Click **Run Install** (creates tables)
+4. Click **Run Song Migration** (imports songs)
+5. Visit `/manage/setup` (create admin account)
+
+#### One-Shot Alternative
+
+```bash
+mysql -u user -p ihymns < appWeb/.sql/.fulldata/ihymns-full.sql
+```
+
+### JSON Fallback Mode
+
+When MySQL is unavailable, the application automatically falls back to reading `data/songs.json`:
+
+| Feature | MySQL Mode | JSON Fallback |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Song browsing & search | FULLTEXT index | Fuse.js client-side |
+| Popular songs | Server view counts | Client localStorage history |
+| Browse by theme (tags) | Tag tables | Hidden (no data) |
+| Song view tracking | tblSongHistory | Silently skipped |
+| User accounts | Full auth system | Not available |
+| Translation links | tblSongTranslations | From songs.json |
+| Song editor | Full CRUD | Read-only |
+| Offline downloads | Bulk API | Per-song fallback |
+
+API endpoints gracefully return empty arrays with `fallback: true` flag when the database is unavailable.
+
+### Database Schema Overview
+
+**Song Data (6 tables):**
+
+| Table | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `tblSongbooks` | Songbook definitions (CP, JP, MP, SDAH, CH, Misc) |
+| `tblSongs` | Core metadata + `LyricsText` for FULLTEXT search |
+| `tblSongWriters` | Lyricist credits (many-to-one) |
+| `tblSongComposers` | Composer credits (many-to-one) |
+| `tblSongComponents` | Verses, choruses with lyrics as JSON lines array |
+| `tblSongTranslations` | Links songs to translations in other languages |
+
+**Discovery & Community (4 tables):**
+
+| Table | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `tblSongHistory` | View tracking for popular songs ranking |
+| `tblSongTags` | Thematic tag definitions (Easter, Advent, etc.) |
+| `tblSongTagMap` | Song-to-tag mapping |
+| `tblSongRequests` | User-submitted song requests |
+
+**Languages (1 table):**
+
+| Table | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `tblLanguages` | 14 supported languages with text direction (ltr/rtl) |
+
+**User Accounts & Access (10+ tables):**
+
+| Table | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `tblUsers` | Accounts with role-based access |
+| `tblUserGroups` | Version channel access (Alpha/Beta/RC/RTW) |
+| `tblSessions` / `tblApiTokens` | Admin panel sessions and API auth tokens |
+| `tblAccessTiers` | Content gating levels (public → pro) |
+| `tblOrganisations` | Church/organisation licensing |
+| `tblUserSetlists` | Cross-device setlist sync |
+| `tblActivityLog` | Audit trail |
+
+Full schema: `appWeb/.sql/schema.sql` (30+ tables, ~50 KB)
+
+### Key API Endpoints
+
+| Endpoint | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| `?action=bulk_songs&songbook=X` | Bulk download: all rendered HTML for a songbook in one response |
+| `?action=songs_json` | Full songs.json export with ETag caching |
+| `?action=song_translations&id=X` | Bidirectional translation lookup |
+| `?action=popular_songs&period=month` | Popular songs by view count |
+| `?action=tags` | All thematic tags |
+| `?page=song&id=X` | Rendered song page HTML (cached by service worker) |
+
+### File Structure
+
+```text
+appWeb/
+├── .auth/
+│   ├── .htaccess                      # Blocks web access
+│   ├── db_credentials.example.php     # Template (tracked in git)
+│   └── db_credentials.php             # Credentials (NOT in git)
+├── .sql/
+│   ├── schema.sql                     # Full MySQL schema
+│   ├── install.php                    # Interactive table installer
+│   ├── migrate-json.php              # JSON → MySQL migration
+│   ├── migrate-users.php             # User/setlist migration
+│   ├── cleanup.php                    # Token/session cleanup
+│   ├── backup.php                     # Database backup
+│   └── .fulldata/
+│       ├── generate-full-sql.php      # One-shot SQL generator
+│       └── ihymns-full.sql            # Pre-built full SQL (~6.8 MB)
+└── public_html/
+    ├── includes/
+    │   ├── db_mysql.php               # MySQLi connection factory
+    │   └── SongData.php               # Song data (MySQL + JSON fallback)
+    └── manage/
+        ├── setup.php                  # Initial admin setup
+        └── setup-database.php         # Web DB admin dashboard
+```
+
+### Troubleshooting
+
+| Issue | Solution |
+| --- | --- |
+| "Database credentials file not found" | Copy `db_credentials.example.php` to `db_credentials.php` |
+| "Failed to connect to MySQL" | Check host, port, username, password in credentials file |
+| "Unknown database 'ihymns'" | Create the database: `CREATE DATABASE ihymns CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;` |
+| "Table already exists" | Normal — the installer uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` |
+| "Migration failed — all changes rolled back" | Check error message; fix and re-run |
+| Popular Songs shows "Loading..." | Database required for server-side view tracking; falls back to localStorage |
+| Browse by Theme missing | Tags must be populated in `tblSongTags` via the admin tools |
+
+### Architecture: Why MySQL + JSON Fallback?
+
+MySQL is the primary store for:
+1. **Full-text search** — FULLTEXT indexes on title and lyrics
+2. **Concurrent writes** — Multiple editors can safely modify data
+3. **User accounts** — Relational storage for users, groups, permissions
+4. **View tracking** — Popular songs ranking from `tblSongHistory`
+5. **Tags & translations** — Structured relational data
+
+JSON fallback ensures the app works everywhere:
+- Shared hosting without MySQL
+- Development without database setup
+- Offline via service worker cached `songs.json`
+- The PWA client always has `songs.json` for Fuse.js fuzzy search
+
+### User Groups & Version Access
+
+| Group | Alpha | Beta | RC | RTW |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Developers | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
+| Beta Testers | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
+| RC Testers | No | No | Yes | Yes |
+| Public | No | No | No | Yes |
+
+Users inherit access from their group. The app checks group permissions to gate access to deployment channels (Alpha = `dev.ihymns.app`, Beta = `beta.ihymns.app`).
+
+---
+
+## Content Access Tiers & CCLI Licensing
+
+### Overview
+
+iHymns uses a tiered content access system to control what songs, media, and features a user can access. Tiers are defined in `tblAccessTiers` and assigned per-user (`tblUsers.AccessTier`) or per-organisation (`tblOrganisations.LicenceType`).
+
+**Content gating is OFF by default** (`content_gating_enabled=0` in `tblAppSettings`). Set to `1` to enforce tier restrictions.
+
+### Default Tiers
+
+| Tier | Level | Lyrics | Copyrighted | Audio | MIDI DL | PDF DL | Offline | CCLI Req'd |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| **Public** | 0 | Yes | - | - | - | - | - | - |
+| **Free** | 10 | Yes | Yes | - | - | - | - | - |
+| **CCLI** | 20 | Yes | Yes | Yes | - | - | - | Yes |
+| **Premium** | 30 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | - |
+| **Pro** | 40 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | - |
+
+Each tier inherits all capabilities of lower tiers. The `Level` column determines the hierarchy — higher level = more access.
+
+### Tier Resolution (Personal vs Organisation)
+
+A user's **effective tier** is the **highest** of:
+
+1. Their personal `AccessTier` on `tblUsers`
+2. Any tier inherited from their organisation memberships
+
+For example:
+
+- User has personal tier `free` (level 10)
+- User belongs to a church with `ihymns_pro` licence (maps to `premium`, level 30)
+- **Effective tier = `premium`** (the higher of the two)
+
+This is resolved by `resolveEffectiveTier()` in `ccli_validator.php`.
+
+### Organisation Licence → Tier Mapping
+
+| Org LicenceType | Maps to Tier |
+| --- | --- |
+| `none` | public |
+| `ihymns_basic` | free |
+| `ccli` | ccli |
+| `ihymns_pro` / `premium` | premium |
+| `pro` | pro |
+
+### CCLI Licence Numbers
+
+CCLI (Christian Copyright Licensing International) licence numbers are:
+- 5–8 digit numeric identifiers
+- Assigned to churches/organisations for copyright compliance
+- Validated via `validateCcliNumber()` in `ccli_validator.php`
+- Stored on `tblUsers.CcliNumber` with `CcliVerified` flag
+
+When a user enters a valid CCLI number:
+1. Format validated (5-8 digits, numeric only)
+2. Stored and marked as verified
+3. If user is on `free` tier, auto-upgraded to `ccli`
+
+### Adding New Tiers
+
+To create a new tier:
+
+```sql
+INSERT INTO tblAccessTiers (Name, DisplayName, Level, Description,
+    CanViewLyrics, CanViewCopyrighted, CanPlayAudio,
+    CanDownloadMidi, CanDownloadPdf, CanOfflineSave, RequiresCcli)
+VALUES ('church_basic', 'Church Basic', 15,
+    'Church plan with copyrighted songs and audio.',
+    1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0);
+```
+
+Then update `checkTierAccess()` in `ccli_validator.php` to include the new tier in the capability matrix, and add the tier name to the `$validTiers` array in the `admin_set_user_tier` API endpoint.
+
+### Setting Up Pricing / Prerequisites
+
+Pricing and payment integration are managed via `tblUserPurchases`:
+
+| Column | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `ProductType` | `tier_upgrade`, `songbook_unlock`, `feature_unlock`, `subscription` |
+| `TierGranted` | Which tier this purchase unlocks |
+| `Amount` / `Currency` | Payment amount (GBP default) |
+| `Status` | `active`, `expired`, `refunded`, `cancelled` |
+| `ExpiresAt` | NULL for one-off purchases; date for subscriptions |
+
+To set up a paid tier:
+
+1. Create the tier in `tblAccessTiers`
+2. Configure your payment processor (Stripe, PayPal, etc.)
+3. On successful payment, insert a row into `tblUserPurchases`
+4. Update the user's `AccessTier` to the purchased tier
+
+### Restricting Media Access
+
+Audio playback, MIDI downloads, and PDF sheet music downloads are controlled by tier capabilities:
+
+| Media Type | Controlled By | API Check |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Audio playback (MIDI) | `CanPlayAudio` | `?action=tier_check&check=play_audio` |
+| MIDI file download | `CanDownloadMidi` | `?action=tier_check&check=download_midi` |
+| Sheet music PDF | `CanDownloadPdf` | `?action=tier_check&check=download_pdf` |
+| Offline song save | `CanOfflineSave` | `?action=tier_check&check=offline_save` |
+
+The frontend should call `tier_check` before showing media controls. If denied, show an upgrade prompt with the `upgradeTo` tier from the response.
+
+### Admin Management
+
+Tier management is restricted to **Admin** and **Global Admin** roles only.
+
+**API endpoints (Admin/Global Admin):**
+
+| Endpoint | Method | Description |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `admin_set_user_tier` | POST | Set a user's access tier |
+| `admin_set_user_ccli` | POST | Validate and set a user's CCLI number |
+| `access_tiers` | GET | List all available tiers |
+
+**Web dashboard:** `/manage/setup-database` for database administration.
+
+---
+
+## Admin Portal (`/manage/` + `/admin/` alias)
+
+| Route | Purpose | Entitlement |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `/manage/` | Dashboard (library + activity stats) | `view_admin_dashboard` |
+| `/manage/editor/` | Song editor | `edit_songs` |
+| `/manage/users` | Users + roles | `view_users` / `edit_users` |
+| `/manage/requests` | Song-request triage queue | `review_song_requests` |
+| `/manage/analytics` | Usage analytics with CSV export | `view_analytics` |
+| `/manage/entitlements` | Reassign capabilities to roles | `manage_entitlements` |
+| `/manage/setup-database` | Install, migrate, backup, restore | `run_db_install` etc. |
+| `/manage/login` · `/manage/logout` · `/manage/setup` | Auth flow (session-based) | — |
+
+### Entitlements
+
+Defined in `appWeb/public_html/includes/entitlements.php` (PHP, authoritative) and mirrored in `appWeb/public_html/js/modules/entitlements.js` (UI affordance only). Runtime overrides stored in `tblAppSettings.SettingKey = 'entitlements_overrides'` as JSON and merged over the hardcoded defaults by `effectiveEntitlements()`. Admins edit the mapping at `/manage/entitlements` — the form prevents removing `global_admin` from the `manage_entitlements` entitlement so the editor can never be locked out.
+
+Check PHP: `userHasEntitlement($name, $role)`. Check JS: `userHasEntitlement(name, role)` (same signature).
+
+### Channel Gating
+
+`alpha.ihymns.app` and `beta.ihymns.app` require the `access_alpha` / `access_beta` entitlements respectively. Production (`ihymns.app`) is never gated. Gate logic lives in `includes/channel_gate.php` and runs from `index.php`. The gate page embeds the magic-link sign-in form so users can authenticate without leaving.
+
+### Auth + persistence
+
+- Bearer token stored in both `Authorization: Bearer` header (JS fetches) and as `Set-Cookie: ihymns_auth; Domain=.ihymns.app; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Secure` (cross-subdomain).
+- Sliding 30-day expiry via `slideAuthTokenExpiry()` — bumps `tblApiTokens.ExpiresAt` at most once per day per token.
+- Client `user-auth.js#verify()` only clears credentials on 401/403 (not on any non-ok), so a transient 500 doesn't sign the user out.
+
+### CSRF
+
+Every write-performing admin page (`users`, `setup`, `login`, `setup-database`, `requests`, `entitlements`) uses `csrfToken()` + `validateCsrf()` from `manage/includes/auth.php`. The token is rendered as a hidden input named `csrf_token`.
+
+### Combining with Other Access Controls
+
+Content tiers work alongside other gating mechanisms:
+
+1. **Content Restrictions** (`tblContentRestrictions`) — block specific songs/songbooks by org/user/platform
+2. **User Groups** (`tblUserGroups`) — version channel access (Alpha/Beta/RC/RTW)
+3. **Organisation Licences** (`tblContentLicences`) — per-org songbook and feature access
+4. **Tiers** — broad capability levels for media and content types
+
+The most restrictive rule wins when multiple systems overlap.
+
+---
+
+## 🤖 Auto-Merge for Alpha PRs
+
+PRs whose **base branch is `alpha`** are automatically merged once all required status checks (and reviews, if configured) pass. PRs targeting `main`, `beta`, or any other branch are **not** affected.
+
+### How it works
+
+The workflow `.github/workflows/auto-merge-alpha.yml` triggers on `pull_request` events scoped to `branches: [alpha]`. It runs a single command:
+
+```bash
+gh pr merge --auto --squash "$PR_URL"
+```
+
+This flips on GitHub's native **auto-merge** flag for the PR. GitHub itself then watches the PR and merges it the moment all gates are green. If checks fail, the PR stays open — nothing is merged.
+
+Drafts are skipped (`if: github.event.pull_request.draft == false`) because GitHub refuses to enable auto-merge on draft PRs.
+
+### One-time repo configuration (required)
+
+The workflow alone is not enough — auto-merge is a repo-level feature:
+
+1. **Settings → General → Pull Requests → "Allow auto-merge"** must be ticked. Without this, the `gh pr merge --auto` call errors out.
+2. **Settings → Branches → Branch protection rule for `alpha`** should require at least one status check (e.g. the `CI Lint & Validation` job from `test.yml`). Without required checks, auto-merge has nothing to wait on and would merge instantly.
+3. (Optional) Add **"Require pull request reviews"** to the same `alpha` branch protection rule if you want a human approval gate. Auto-merge respects it.
+
+### Knobs to tweak
+
+| What | Where | How |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Merge strategy | `run:` line in `auto-merge-alpha.yml` | `--squash` → `--merge` (merge commit) or `--rebase` |
+| Add more target branches | `on.pull_request.branches` | Add entries, e.g. `- beta` |
+| Restrict to specific authors | Add `if:` to the job | e.g. `github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]'` |
+| Disable for a single PR | Anywhere with write access | `gh pr merge --disable-auto <PR>` |
+
+### How to verify it works
+
+Open a test PR from any branch into `alpha`. Within ~30s the workflow runs, and the PR's merge box will show **"Auto-merge enabled"**. Push a failing commit → it stays unmerged. Fix it → it merges itself.
+
+### Troubleshooting
+
+- **Workflow fails with "auto-merge is not allowed"** → Repo setting #1 above is off.
+- **PR merges immediately with no checks** → No required status checks on `alpha` branch protection.
+- **Workflow doesn't run** → PR is a draft, or its base isn't `alpha`. Both are intentional.
+- **PR has merge conflicts** → Auto-merge waits silently until conflicts are resolved.
+
+---
+
+## 🔗 External Links System (#833) and Auto-Detect Module (#841)
+
+### Schema
+
+External links live in a controlled-vocabulary registry plus per-entity
+sibling tables:
+
+| Table | Owns the relationship for |
+| --- | --- |
+| `tblExternalLinkTypes` | The seeded provider registry (~37 types: Wikipedia, Hymnary.org, MusicBrainz, IMSLP, Spotify, YouTube, …) — see `migrate-external-links.php` |
+| `tblSongbookExternalLinks` | `tblSongbooks` ↔ link types |
+| `tblSongExternalLinks` | `tblSongs` ↔ link types |
+| `tblCreditPersonExternalLinks` | `tblCreditPeople` ↔ link types |
+| `tblWorkExternalLinks` | `tblWorks` ↔ link types (#840) |
+
+`tblExternalLinkTypes.AppliesTo` is a `SET('song','songbook','person','work')`
+that decides which entity types each provider applies to. The Works
+migration (`migrate-works.php`) widens this set + seeds the `'work'`
+flag on the appropriate provider rows.
+
+Per-entity rows carry: `Url` (≤ 2048 chars), `Note`, `SortOrder`,
+`Verified`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`. FK on the entity is
+`ON DELETE CASCADE`; FK on the link type is `ON DELETE RESTRICT`
+(so the registry can't be accidentally trimmed under live data).
+
+### Read path
+
+`SongData::_externalLinksMap($entityType, $keys)` is the generic
+helper. Probe-gated on the relevant `tblXxxExternalLinks` table;
+joins `tblExternalLinkTypes` and excludes rows where `IsActive = 0`
+(soft delete). Returns a map keyed by Abbreviation / SongId /
+CreditPersonId.
+
+### URL → Provider auto-detect (#841)
+
+Single source of truth in
+`appWeb/public_html/js/modules/external-link-detect.js`, exposed on
+`window.iHymnsLinkDetect`:
+
+- `detectFromUrl(url)` → slug or `null`
+- `slugToOptionValue(selectEl, slug)` → numeric option value or `''`
+- `attachAutoDetect(rowEl, opts)` → teardown function
+
+Loaded on every `/manage/*` page by `manage/includes/head-libs.php`,
+so each per-page row builder calls
+`window.iHymnsLinkDetect.attachAutoDetect(card)` and inherits the
+behaviour without an extra script tag.
+
+**Adding a new provider:** append a rule to the `RULES` array in
+the module. That's the only place — every consumer inherits.
+
+**Manual-choice override:** `data-user-picked="1"` is stamped on the
+`<select>` once the user changes it explicitly. The detector reads
+that attr and bails when set.
+
+---
+
+## 🎼 Works (#840) — composition grouping
+
+`tblWorks` groups multiple `tblSongs` rows representing the same
+composition across different songbooks / arrangements / translations.
+Mirrors the MusicBrainz Work ↔ Recording relationship.
+
+### Schema
+
+```
+tblWorks
+  Id               PK
+  ParentWorkId     self-FK, ON DELETE SET NULL → unlimited nesting
+  Iswc             CHAR(15), UNIQUE, optional
+  Title            VARCHAR(255)
+  Slug             VARCHAR(80), UNIQUE
+  Notes            TEXT
+  CreatedAt / UpdatedAt
+
+tblWorkSongs
+  WorkId, SongId   composite PK
+  IsCanonical      flag (zero or one per Work, by convention)
+  SortOrder
+  Note
+
+tblWorkExternalLinks
+  same shape as the per-entity link tables (see above).
+```
+
+### Read path
+
+`SongData::_worksMap($songIds)` bulk-attaches `works` to song rows;
+each Work entry includes its `members` (sibling versions across the
+catalogue) and Work-level `links`. `SongData::getWork($slugOrId)`
+returns the full Work payload for the public `/work/<slug>` page.
+
+### Cycle prevention
+
+Application-side at update time (`manage/works.php`'s
+`$cycleSafe` closure walks the parent chain with a depth cap of 64).
+MySQL has no native cycle constraint and we don't otherwise rely on
+stored procedures, so this is the cheapest correct guard. The depth
+cap doubles as a "table somehow already inconsistent" circuit-breaker.
+
+---
+
+## 📱 Admin list-view responsive convention (#842)
+
+Every admin list table that opts into `.admin-table-responsive` gets
+a column-priority hide-on-narrow rule from the global stylesheet
+(`appWeb/public_html/css/admin.css`).
+
+Mark each `<th>` AND its corresponding `<td>` with one of:
+
+| Priority | Hides at |
+| --- | --- |
+| `data-col-priority="primary"` | never |
+| `data-col-priority="secondary"` | ≤ 768 px |
+| `data-col-priority="tertiary"` | ≤ 992 px |
+
+When adding a new admin list page: add the class to the `<table>`
+and the `data-col-priority` attribute to every `<th>` and `<td>`.
+That's it — no per-page CSS.
+
+The opt-in shape (rather than auto-applying to every `.table`) keeps
+the blast radius zero on existing pages while we roll the convention
+forward.
+
+Pages currently opted in: Credit People, Songbooks, Songbook Series,
+Works.
+
+---
+
+Last updated: 2026-05-04

- feat(catalogue): **Works — composition grouping** (#840) — new top-level `tblWorks` entity that groups multiple `tblSongs` rows representing the same underlying composition across different songbooks / arrangements / translations. Mirrors the MusicBrainz Work ↔ Recording relationship. Optional ISWC, optional notes, unlimited parent / child nesting (cycle-prevention enforced server-side at update time). New `/work/<slug>` public page with categorised "Find this work elsewhere" panel, and a "Part of work" + sibling-version list on every song page that belongs to one. New `/manage/works` admin CRUD page gated on the `manage_works` entitlement.
- feat(admin): **URL → provider auto-detect** (#841) for the External-Links card-list editor. Paste a Wikipedia / YouTube / Spotify / etc. URL and the provider dropdown auto-selects the matching registry entry. Single global module (`js/modules/external-link-detect.js`) loaded on every `/manage/*` page; one-line `attachAutoDetect(rowEl)` wiring per consumer. Adding a new provider is a one-line append to the `RULES` array. 30+ providers covered, full unit-test coverage in `tests/test-external-link-detect.js`.
- refactor(admin): **responsive list-view convention** (#842) — `.admin-table-responsive` + `data-col-priority="primary|secondary|tertiary"` lets pages opt into a column-priority hide-on-narrow rule. Below 768 px secondary + tertiary columns hide; below 992 px tertiary only. Pages opted in this PR: Credit People (the original phone-clipping motivator), Songbooks, Songbook Series, Works. Convention documented in `DEV_NOTES.md`.
- docs: **comprehensive refresh** (#843) — visitor in-app help adds an "External links & Works" section; admin in-app help adds Works, External Links and Mobile Admin sections; OpenAPI spec adds `Work` schema + `ExternalLink` shared schema + `/api?action=work&slug=…` endpoint; `DEV_NOTES.md` documents the external-links data shape, Works schema and the responsive convention.

- feat(songs): **cross-book counterparts** (#807)

schemas:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Core domain models
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Song:
      type: object
      description: Complete song object with lyrics components
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          description: "Unique song ID in BOOK-NUMBER format"
          example: CP-0202
        number:
          type: integer
          description: Song number within the songbook
          example: 202
        title:
          type: string
          description: Song title
          example: Amazing Grace
        songbook:
          type: string
          description: Songbook abbreviation
          example: CP
        songbookName:
          type: string
          description: Full songbook name
          example: Christian Praise
        language:
          type: string
          description: Language code
          example: en
        copyright:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: Copyright information
        ccli:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: CCLI license number
        verified:
          type: boolean
          description: Whether the song lyrics have been verified
        lyricsPublicDomain:
          type: boolean
          description: Whether the lyrics are in the public domain
        musicPublicDomain:
          type: boolean
          description: Whether the music is in the public domain
        hasAudio:
          type: boolean
          description: Whether an audio recording is available
        hasSheetMusic:
          type: boolean
          description: Whether sheet music is available
        writers:
          type: array
          items:

          description: Lyricist / writer names
