Songbooks

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Songbooks are the top-level container — every song lives in exactly one. This page is where you create, name, colour, and order them. +

+

Per-songbook fields

+
+
Abbreviation
Short identifier (e.g. HYM). Unique. Max 10 chars, alphanumeric. This is the natural key referenced by every song.
+
Name
Friendly name (e.g. "Methodist Hymnal").
+
Display order
Numeric sort key — lower numbers appear first in the app.
+
Colour
Hex code (#RRGGBB) used as the songbook tile colour on the home page. Leave blank to let the system auto-pick a tone from the current theme palette (#677) — the result is consistent with the rest of the UI and changes with the user's chosen theme.
+
Official flag
Marks "real" published hymnals vs. user-curated collections / pseudo-songbooks. Used by the home-page filter to separate the two surfaces.
+
Publisher / Publication year / Copyright
Issuing body, year of publication, and the copyright statement. Optional, surface in search and reports.
+
Affiliation
Issuing organisation, drawn from a curated registry (#670). Type to search; new affiliations get added on save. Use this rather than free-text Publisher when the same organisation issues multiple songbooks.
+
Language (IETF BCP 47)
The songbook's primary language as a composite IETF tag (#673 / #681) — same picker as the song editor, with three sub-fields: Language (required), Script (optional — only when the script differs from the language default), and Region (optional — e.g. en-GB vs en-US). Leave blank for multi-lingual collections.
+
Online links — Official website / Internet Archive / Wikipedia (#672)
Free-text URLs. Used as outbound references on the songbook detail page so users can verify the source.
+
Authority identifiers — WikiData ID, OCLC, OCN, LCP, ISBN, ARK, ISNI, VIAF, LCCN, LC Class (#672)
Standard cataloguing identifiers from major library and authority systems. All optional. Useful for cross-referencing and de-duplicating against external catalogues.
+
+

Renaming an abbreviation

+

+ Abbreviations are the natural key, so renaming is opt-in: you must tick the "Also rename song references" checkbox to cascade the rename to every song that uses it. Without that checkbox, songs keep the old abbreviation and orphan from the renamed songbook. +

+

Colour picker

+

+ The Colour field accepts a 7-char #RRGGBB hex value (#715). The browser-native colour picker writes the canonical lower-case hex back into the text field when you confirm a swatch — handy if you want to copy the value into another tool. Leave the field blank to let the system auto-pick a tone the catalogue isn't already using; the next save fills the field in for you. +

+

Auto-colour bulk action

+

+ Two destructive-but-recoverable buttons live at the top of the songbook list (#716): +

+
+
Auto-fill blank colours
+
Walks every songbook; rows with NULL or non-#RRGGBB colours get a fresh palette pick. Existing valid hex values are left alone — idempotent, safe to re-run.
+
Reassign every colour
+
Overwrites every Colour value, regardless of whether it was set already. Gated by typing the literal phrase REASSIGN ALL — defence-in-depth so a stray click never re-themes the whole catalogue.
+
+

Cascade delete

+

+ The default Delete refuses if any song still references the songbook abbreviation. Admin / global_admin can use Cascade delete instead, which removes the songbook AND every song in it AND every credit / tag / chord / translation that referenced those songs (#706). Server-side typed-confirmation gate: the curator must type the songbook abbreviation exactly. The FK chain handles the rest atomically. +

+
+ Gotcha: Deleting a songbook does not delete its songs unless you use Cascade delete. The standard UI refuses if any song still references its abbreviation; reassign or delete those songs first. +
+
+ Tip: The home-page tile grid (#678) shows official hymnals first, with a language filter (#679 / #736 v2) that lets users pick which languages to show across both songbook tiles AND individual song listings (search, popular, recently-viewed). Multi-select is supported; signed-in users get the choice persisted to their account and synced across devices. The Misc pseudo-songbook is always pinned to the bottom of the grid (#717) regardless of DisplayOrder — it's a catch-all and should never out-rank a curated hymnal. Songbooks AND songs without a Language field always show, regardless of the filter — useful for catch-all collections. +
+
+ +
+

Credit People

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ A registry of every named person credited on a song — writers, composers, arrangers, adaptors, translators. Lets you fix the “J. Newton vs John Newton” problem in one place instead of in every song that mentions them. +

+

Key actions

+
+
Add
Pre-register a canonical spelling (with optional birth/death info, IPI numbers, external links) so it appears in the editor's autocomplete from day one.
+
Edit
Update biographical info, links, IPI numbers. Editing a name applies to all songs that cite it.
+
Rename
Change the canonical name and cascade the change atomically across every song that cites it.
+
Merge
Collapse two registry entries into one. Pick which row survives; all credits on songs are re-pointed to the survivor and the duplicate is deleted.
+
Delete
Remove from the registry. Refuses by default if any song still cites them; force-delete is available behind a confirmation.
+
View Songs
Modal showing every song that cites a person, grouped by role (writer, composer, …).
+
+
+ Gotcha: Rename and Merge are atomic — either every credit on every song updates, or none does. Half-finished states are not possible. +
+

Bulk promote (#846)

+

+ When a fresh deployment has hundreds of typed credit names that haven't been registered, click Bulk promote with fuzzy-match on the Credit People page header. The bulk page surfaces every name cited on at least one song that doesn't have a registry row, scores each against the existing registry rows (and against other candidates), and lets you pick per-row: Register as new, Merge into existing (re-points every credit on every song to the canonical row's name), or Skip. The whole submit runs in a single transaction with one bulk_run_id on the audit log so you can review the run as a unit. +

+
+ +
+

Works

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ A Work groups multiple tblSongs rows that represent the same underlying composition across different songbooks / arrangements / translations — mirrors the MusicBrainz Work ↔ Recording relationship. So Amazing Grace, which appears in dozens of hymnals under slightly different titles, lives as one Work with each songbook entry as a member. +

+

Key actions

+
+
Create
Title + slug (auto from title) + optional ISWC + optional parent Work + optional notes. Members are added via the Edit modal once the row exists.
+
Edit
Add / remove member songs (typeahead over the whole catalogue), mark one as canonical, set sort order, attach external links (the provider dropdown auto-detects from the URL).
+
Delete
Memberships and external links cascade away with the Work. Child Works (if any) orphan — their ParentWorkId goes to NULL — rather than cascade-delete.
+
+

Nesting

+

+ Works can be nested without limit: an original Work can have child Works for derivative arrangements, translations, choral versions, etc., each of which can in turn have its own children. Cycles are blocked server-side at update time (no Work can become its own ancestor). +

+

ISWC

+

+ The ISWC (T-NNN.NNN.NNN-C) is the international identifier for a musical composition, registered with CISAC societies (BMI, ASCAP, PRS, …). It's optional — many traditional hymns predate the system, and many newer compositions haven't been registered. When supplied, the field shape-validates and canonicalises to the standard format. +

+
+ Gotcha: The same song can belong to multiple Works (e.g. a medley arrangement that quotes two compositions), but it's rare and usually a misclassification. The list view's "Members" column is the quickest sanity check. +
+
+ +
+

External Links

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Songs, Songbooks, Credit People and Works all support a card-list editor for external links — controlled-vocabulary providers (Wikipedia, Hymnary.org, Spotify, IMSLP, MusicBrainz, etc.) backed by tblExternalLinkTypes. Each link carries an optional Note and a curator-set Verified flag. +

+

URL auto-detect (#841)

+

+ Paste a URL into the URL field of any external-link row and the provider dropdown auto-selects the matching registry entry — Wikipedia detects Wikipedia, YouTube detects YouTube, Spotify detects Spotify, etc. The detector respects manual choices: if you pick a provider before pasting, your choice wins. +

+

+ The detector lives in a single global module — js/modules/external-link-detect.js — loaded on every /manage/* page. Every consumer (Songbook editor, Works editor, Credit People editor as it's added) inherits automatically. +

+

URL patterns (#845)

+

+ Provider rules live in the tblExternalLinkPatterns table — curator-editable at /manage/external-link-types. Add a new provider, sub-domain or path-prefix-discriminated rule (e.g. musicbrainz.org/work/) at any time without a code deploy. Lower priority numbers win, so put more-specific patterns first. The JS module falls back to a bundled rule list on pre-migration deployments so behaviour stays consistent during rollout. +

+

Categories

+

Links group on the public site under: Official, Information, Read, Sheet music, Listen, Watch, Purchase, Authority, Social, Other. The seeded type registry decides which category each provider belongs to; curators don't pick the category — it's derived from the type.

+
+ +
+

Mobile admin (responsive list views)

+

+ Admin list pages opt into a column-priority responsive convention (#842). Tag the table .admin-table-responsive, then mark each <th> + <td> with data-col-priority="primary", "secondary", or "tertiary". Below 992px tertiary columns hide; below 768px secondary columns hide too. Primary columns are always visible. +

+

+ Pages currently opted in: Credit People, Songbooks, Songbook Series, Works. The convention is documented in DEV_NOTES.md; rolling it forward to the remaining list pages is a per-page cosmetic change with zero CSS work. +

+

+

Content Restrictions

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Rule-based access control. Each rule says "for this thing, on this platform / for this user / when this licence is or isn't held, allow or deny." +

+

Anatomy of a rule

+
+
Entity
What's being restricted: a single song, an entire songbook, or a feature like audio playback.
+
Restriction type
How: block by platform / block by user / block by org / require a licence / require an org membership.
+
Target
The thing on the other side of the rule: a platform name, user ID, org ID, or licence type.
+
Effect
Allow or Deny when this rule fires.
+
Priority (0–1000)
Higher beats lower. At equal priority, Deny beats Allow.
+
Reason
Free-text note. Strongly recommended — future-you will thank present-you.
+
+

Common patterns

+
    +
  • Hide a song from a specific platform — block_platform with target = platform name.
    • +
  • Restrict copyrighted songs to CCLI holders — require_licence with target = ccli.
    • +
  • Allow only one user to see a draft song — block_user for everyone (low priority) plus an Allow rule (high priority) for that user.
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: Rules are evaluated at request time. Changes take effect on the next page load — but data already cached on a user's device may lag a few minutes. +
+
+ +
+

Access Tiers

+

+ global_admin +

+

+ Tiers are bundles of capabilities (view lyrics, view copyrighted lyrics, play audio, download MIDI, download PDF, save offline, requires CCLI). Every user is assigned one tier, which controls what UI controls they see in the main app. +

+

Default tiers (seeded at install)

+
    +
  • public — lyrics only, public-domain only.
    • +
  • free — lyrics, no audio, no copyrighted content.
    • +
  • ccli — lyrics + copyrighted, but only if the user's organisation has a CCLI licence number.
    • +
  • premium — everything except offline.
    • +
  • pro — everything.
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: A tier's machine name is set on creation and never changes. To “rename” a tier, create a new one, reassign users to it, then delete the old one. +
+
+ + + +
+

Users

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Manage every user account: create accounts, assign roles, deactivate, reset passwords, change tiers. +

+

Key actions

+
    +
  • Create — username (min 3 chars, lowercase letters / digits / dot / hyphen / underscore), password REDACTED 8 chars), display name, role, tier.
    • +
  • Edit profile — display name, email, tier.
    • +
  • Change role — admins can only assign roles at or below their own; only a global admin can promote someone to admin or global admin.
    • +
  • Activate / Deactivate — deactivated users cannot sign in.
    • +
  • Reset password — sets a new password REDACTED (the user is not auto-signed-out from existing sessions).
    • +
  • Delete — permanent. Their setlists, song revisions, and activity entries remain (linked by user ID) for audit reasons.
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: You cannot deactivate your own account. +
+
+ Gotcha: Username is set on creation and is immutable. Display name can be changed any time. +

User Groups

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Logical buckets of users for shared release-channel access (Alpha / Beta / RC / RTW). Useful for “who sees pre-release content?” without managing flags per-user. +

+

Key actions

+
    +
  • Create a group with a name, description, and four channel flags.
    • +
  • Two-pane membership editor: drag users between “Available” and “In group.”
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: One group per user. Re-assigning moves them; there's no “in two groups at once.” +
+
+ Role vs Group (#642): these names sound similar but they're independent concepts. +
    +
  • User Role (Curator / Admin / Global Admin) controls which Manage pages a user can access. The four roles are hard-coded today; new roles need a code change.
    • +
  • User Group controls which release channel a user sees on the public site (Alpha / Beta / RC / RTW). Group membership is freely admin-managed via this page.
    • +
+ Don't expect adding a User Group to grant Manage access — for that, change the user's Role from User Management. Issue #642 tracks the rationalisation. +

Organisations

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Churches, denominations, schools. Group users together and attach a single licence (CCLI / iHymns Pro / iHymns Basic) to that group instead of to each user. +

+

Per-org fields

+
+
Slug
URL-safe identifier (auto-derived from name; you can override). Unique.
+
Parent org
Optional; lets you build a denomination → diocese → church chain. Licences inherit downward.
+
Licence type / number
none, ihymns_basic, ihymns_pro, or ccli. CCLI requires a licence number for audit.
+
Active flag
Inactive orgs are kept in the database but their licence stops counting toward members.
+
+

Membership

+

Two-pane picker, same shape as User Groups. Each member also gets a sub-role: member (no extra perms), admin (can manage other members), or owner (full control of the org).

+
+ Gotcha: An org cannot be its own parent (and we block circular chains in general). +
+
+ +
+

My Organisations

+

+ org admin + org owner + admin + global_admin +

+

+ The org-admin surface (#707, #726). Visible to anyone who holds an admin or owner row in tblOrganisationMembers for at least one organisation — they don't need system-admin role to see this page. System admins see it too, scoped to every org. +

+

What it does

+
    +
  • Lists every organisation the current user can manage.
    • +
  • For each, shows the member roster with role badges and the licence rows on file.
    • +
  • Inline forms for the six edit actions described below — you don't need /manage/organisations for routine org-admin work.
    • +
+

Member actions

+
+
Add member
Free-text identifier — type a username OR an email, the server resolves to a tblUsers.Id. New member rows pick a sub-role (member / admin / owner).
+
Change member role
Inline picker per row.
+
Remove member
You can't remove yourself unless you're also a system admin — prevents accidental org lock-out. Ask a co-admin.
+
+

Licence actions

+
+
Add licence
Per-row licence types: ccli, mrl, ihymns_basic, ihymns_pro, custom. INSERT-on-conflict-UPDATE so re-adding the same type updates number / expiry / notes in place.
+
Change licence
Edit number, expiry date, active flag, notes. Type is immutable on a row — to switch types, remove and re-add.
+
Remove licence
Drops the row. Belt-and-braces ownership check on the server.
+
+

Row-level gate

+

+ Every action runs userCanActOnOrg($userId, $orgId) server-side before any mutation, regardless of whether the call came from the form or a crafted POST. A licence_id from one org can never be edited via an org_id you happen to admin elsewhere. +

+
+ Gotcha: System admins (admin / global_admin) bypass the row-level gate by default. The audit log records the action under org_admin.<verb> regardless, so the timeline reads as one surface. +
+
+ +
+

Entitlements

+

+ global_admin +

+

+ The fine-grained permission map. Every admin action is gated by an entitlement (e.g. edit_songs, verify_songs, manage_songbooks). This page lets you change which roles hold which entitlements, overriding the hard-coded defaults. +

+

When to use it

+
    +
  • Promote a single privilege to a role that doesn't normally have it (e.g. let editors run the CCLI report).
    • +
  • Demote a privilege you want to lock down (e.g. take delete_songs away from admins, leave it with global admins only).
    • +
  • Reset to defaults if you've gone too far — the “Reset” button restores the hard-coded baseline.
    • +
+
+ Gotcha: This is a nuclear tool. A bad change is global, immediate, and visible to everyone on next page load. Make small changes and verify before moving on. +
+
+ Gotcha: The page enforces one safety guard: manage_entitlements itself can never be removed from global_admin, so you can't lock yourself out of the page that re-grants access. +
+

+ admin + global_admin +

Exporting

Each panel has a CSV download button that respects the current window.

Tips

Data Health

+

+ global_admin +

+

+ Confirms that MySQL is the authoritative source for every kind of data, and lets you safely disconnect the legacy fallbacks (the original songs.json, the SQLite user database, the file-system setlist share directory) so the app stops checking them. +

+

Workflow

+
    +
  1. Read the row counts at the top to confirm MySQL has the data you expect.
    2. +
  2. Click Disconnect next to a fallback. The file is renamed to .disabled, not deleted — you can restore it manually if needed.
    3. +
  3. Reload the main app to confirm everything still works without the fallback.

Activity Log

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Every action that mutates data (creates, edits, deletes, sign-ins, sign-outs, role changes, etc.) writes a row here. Searchable, filterable, exportable. +

+

Filters

+
    +
  • User — username or email substring.
    • +
  • Action / Result / Entity type — pick from a list.
    • +
  • Entity ID — the thing that was acted on.
    • +
  • Request ID — trace every row that came from a single browser request (useful when debugging a multi-step action).
    • +
  • Time window — 1 / 7 / 30 / 90 / 365 days.
    • +
  • Free text — matches the action name and entity ID. Use the specific filters for everything else.
    • +
+

CSV export

+

Respects every active filter; capped at 10 000 rows per download.

+

Error capture (#695)

+

+ Server-side exceptions raised by admin POST handlers (the “Database error — check server logs” banner) are mirrored into the activity log with Result='error' and the exception message + class in the Details column. The viewer's Result = error filter is a one-click triage list — you no longer need SSH to see why a save failed. +

+

+ Verb prefix convention: web admin writes <entity>.<verb> (e.g. songbook.create, org.member_add); the public-API surfaces use api.admin.<entity>.<verb> (e.g. api.admin.songbook.create) so timeline readers can tell which surface drove the change. +

+
+ Gotcha: Rows are immutable. There's no edit, no delete — that's the whole point of an audit log. +

Schema Audit

+

+ global_admin +

+

+ Diagnostic page that compares three things: the schema your code expects (schema.sql), the schema your live database actually has, and the migration scripts that bridge the two. Surfaces drift before it bites. +

+

Status meanings

+
+
OK
In code and in DB. Nothing to do.
+
Missing (amber)
In code, not in DB, but a migration covers it. Run that migration on Database Setup.
+
Uncovered (red)
In code, not in DB, and no migration covers it. This is a real bug — an existing install will never get this column. File an issue and write a migration.
+
Orphan
In DB, not in code. Almost always informational — a column you removed from schema.sql is still around in the database. Safe to leave alone.
+
+
+ Gotcha: Schema Audit is read-only. It tells you what's wrong; it never runs ALTER statements itself. +
+
+ +
+

Database Setup

+

+ global_admin +

+

+ The most powerful page in the admin area. Configures the database connection, installs the schema, runs migrations, takes backups, restores from backup. Treat with respect. +

+

Setup workflow on a new install

+
    +
  1. Credentials — fill in host, port, database name, username, password, table prefix. Click Test connection; only save once it goes green.
    2. +
  2. Install schema — creates every table from schema.sql. Idempotent — re-running is safe.
    3. +
  3. Migrate songs JSON — one-time import of data/songs.json into the database.
    4. +
  4. Migrate users / setlists — one-time import from the legacy SQLite + JSON setlist share dir.
    5. +
  5. Run remaining migrations (Account Sync, Songbook Metadata, Credit Fields, Credit People, User Features Catch-up, Activity Log Expand) in the order they appear on the dashboard. Each is idempotent.
    6. +
+

Setup workflow on an existing install

+

+ Re-run Install schema if anything changed in schema.sql (it's safe), then run only the migrations that Schema Audit flagged as missing. Migrations are idempotent — running one that's already been applied just reports “[skip]” for everything. +

+

Apply all pending migrations (#577)

+

+ The Apply all pending migrations button runs every migrate-*.php script in deployment order. Each script is already idempotent, so re-running the bulk action after some have been applied is safe — they no-op individually. +

+

+ If a migration fails mid-run, the dashboard captures the first-failing step and surfaces it in a prominent banner above the (sometimes long, scrollable) output panel (#720), so you don't miss the FAILED line in the noise. Fix the underlying issue and re-run — the steps that succeeded earlier no-op the second time. +

+

Backups

+
    +
  • Backup downloads a SQL dump of the entire database. Keep at least one before running unfamiliar migrations.
    • +
  • Restore uploads a previously downloaded dump and replays it — completely overwrites the current database. Read the warning before you click.
    • +
+

Cleanup

+

Deletes expired API tokens, old login attempts (>30 days), expired email-login codes, etc. Safe to run any time.

+
+ Gotcha: Migrations are not reversible. Always take a backup before running any migration on production. +
+
+ Gotcha: The table prefix is fixed at install time and cannot be changed afterwards. Pick once, live with it. +
+
+ Gotcha: Restore overwrites everything. There is no “merge” option. +
+
+ +
+

Native API surface

+

+ admin + global_admin +

+

+ Every admin verb on this site is also reachable via the public REST API at /api.php?action=<verb> (#719). Native clients (Apple, Android, FireOS) and tooling clients (CI, monitoring, dashboards) can drive the same surfaces the web admin uses without a webview or a separate auth flow. +

+

Auth

+

+ Bearer-token auth via the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Tokens are issued by the existing email-magic-link or password REDACTED flows and live on tblApiTokens. POSTs also need X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest as a CSRF defence (#293). Same role gates as the web admin — admin / global_admin for system-wide write verbs, plus the row-level userCanActOnOrg() check for org-admin endpoints. +

+

What's covered

+
    +
  • Songbooks — create / update / delete / cascade-delete / reorder / auto-colour fill / auto-colour reassign (PR 2a).
    • +
  • Users + Groups + Tiers — full CRUD plus role / activate / password-reset / member-add-remove (PR 2b).
    • +
  • Organisations + My Organisations — system-admin updates plus the six org-admin verbs from this surface (PR 2c).
    • +
  • Credit People — add / update / rename / merge / delete with the same cascade and confirmation gates (PR 2d).
    • +
  • Analytics + Diagnostics — top searches, data health snapshot, schema-audit report, per-migration applied/partial/pending status (PR 2d).
    • +
  • Editor — load / save / save_song / bulk_tag / list_revisions / restore_revision / get_translations / add_translation / remove_translation / song_tags / tag_search / credit_search / user_search / org_search / bulk_import_zip / bulk_import_status (PR 3 docs).
    • +
+

OpenAPI spec

+

+ Every endpoint is documented in /api-docs.yaml as a single OpenAPI 3.0 file. Swagger UI / Stoplight / Redoc all render it cleanly. The spec is the source of truth for the request / response shapes — the web admin uses the helpers underneath, the native clients hit the documented endpoints, both stay in sync because the validators live in shared includes/ files. +

+

Activity-log surface prefix

+

+ API-driven changes write under api.admin.<entity>.<verb> (e.g. api.admin.songbook.create, api.org_admin.licence_change). The Activity Log viewer can show both surfaces side-by-side; the prefix tells you which. +

+
+ Gotcha: Status codes follow REST: 400 (validation), 401, 403 (role gate or row-level refusal), 404, 405 (wrong method), 409 (duplicate key), 422 (cannot delete because dependents exist). Native UIs can render the right toast without parsing the error string. +
+
+ + + +
+

Troubleshooting & FAQs

+ +

“A page that should be in the menu isn't there.”

+

+ You don't have the entitlement for it. The menu only shows pages + you can use. Ask a global admin to grant you the role or + entitlement you need (see Entitlements). +

+ +

“I clicked Save in the editor but my changes aren't there after a refresh.”

+

+ Two common causes: +

+
    +
  • The save was rejected by validation. Look for an error toast at the top right of the editor.
    • +
  • You're editing on one device and viewing on another, with one of them having a service-worker cache that hasn't refreshed yet. A hard refresh (Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-R) typically clears it.
    • +
+ +

“I deleted a song by mistake.”

+

+ Open Revisions Audit, find the song's last edit before the delete, click through to the editor, and use Revisions → Restore. Revisions are kept indefinitely so older deletes are still recoverable. +

+ +

“The dashboard / a /manage page is blank.”

+

+ This is rare. Try a hard refresh first. If still blank, append ?_debug=1&_dev=1 to the URL on Alpha or Beta — the server will print any underlying PHP fatal at the bottom of the response. Capture that and pass it to a developer. +

+ +

“A user reports the main app is showing the wrong songs / locking out features.”

+

+ Check three places, in order: +

+
    +
  1. Their access tier on Users — controls capability gating.
    2. +
  2. Their organisation membership — org licence bubbles down to members.
    3. +
  3. Content Restrictions — rules can block or require things on a per-user / per-org / per-platform basis.
    4. +
+ +

“Two songs / two people / two anything look like duplicates.”

+

+ For people, use Credit People → Merge. For songs, the editor doesn't have a merge tool yet — the safest path is to copy any unique data from one into the other, then delete the duplicate. +

+ +

“Activity Log shows an action I don't recognise. What is it?”

+

+ Activity Log entries follow a verb_noun shape (e.g. create_user, edit_song, delete_organisation_member). The Entity type column tells you what was acted on, the Entity ID is its primary key. Click around — most actions can be reverse-engineered from the noun. +

+ +

“Where do I report a bug or request a feature?”

+

+ Either through your usual channel into the iHymns team, or by e-mail to your iHymns administrator. If you have GitHub access, file an issue at the project repository. +

+
+ +
+
+
+ + + +
